Legacy Pass
Legacy Customers are those that have purchased the adult unlimited, couples unlimited, or adult portion of the family pass at the regular posted rate for the three most recent consecutive years.
Legacy Customers will be locked in at the posted rate paid during the third qualifying year for a period of five additional years.
At the end of the initial five-year period and at the end of each successive five year period, the Legacy Customer's new rate will be adjusted to 5% discount off of the current posted rate and locked in for an additional five-year period.
The Legacy Customer must renew their pass each year to maintain the legacy designation. If the customer fails, for any reason, to renew their pass during a year then they will lose their legacy designation and the next time they purchase a season pass, it would be at the current posted rate.
After losing the Legacy Customer status, the customer may only re-establish their Legacy designation by purchasing a season pass for an additional three consecutive years at the posted rate for each year.

RV Park Rules
1) RV Park stay is limited to 14 consecutive days. You may request to return to the RV Park
after one month.
2) Check-in at 1:00 pm. Check-out at 12:00 pm (noon).
3) RV and Tow vehicle must be in good, clean, operable condition. “Drop offs” are
specifically NOT allowed.
4) Maximum occupancy of six people and two vehicles per site. No vehicles may be
parked in adjacent sites.
5) All noise activities, including loud voices and music, must cease by 10:00 p.m. No
Generators.
6) Pets must be on a leash or penned at all times when outside and must be picked up
after. Dogs and other pets must not be a threat or a nuisance to other park users.
Excessive barking is not allowed. Pets may not be left unattended at the Park.
7) RV sites must be kept clean at all times.
8) Absolutely no black or gray water is to be dumped on the ground. No washing or
repair/maintenance of RVs or vehicles.
9) Fire allowed in fire pits only unless prohibited by fire bans. Small barbecues and gas-
fueled fires are allowed.
10) No sale of cars, boats, vehicles, etc. No yard sales. No businesses shall be operated
from the RV Park.

pages.title: Campground Directory - ReserveAmerica
pages.text:
Campground Directory - ReserveAmerica
Skip to main content
Campground Directory
There are thousands of public and privately-owned campgrounds catering to the needs of millions of campers using tents, travel trailers, motor homes or other types of RVs. Our campground directory will describe each, as to location, season, rates and amenities.
The Followings are the major types of campgrounds:
State Agencies
Colorado Parks and Wildlife
Colorado Parks & Wildlife (CPW) has partnered with Aspira since 1993. In 2018, CPW implemented IPAWS (Integrated Parks and Wildlife System), marking the industry's first fully integrated parks and licensing system. Aspira manages this comprehensive platform that allows users to purchase fishing and hunting licenses, campground reservations, vehicle registrations, hunting reservations, and license draws through a single cart system, serving customers both online and through 400+ license agent locations. A significant enhancement to IPAWS was the 2023 introduction of the Keep Colorado Wild Pass, which integrates with the state's DMV system and has attracted over 2 million participants by offering discounted state park access during vehicle registration renewal.
Connecticut Department of Energy and Environmental Protection
A partner for over 25 years, Connecticut offers campgrounds in thirteen state parks or forests with over 1,400 campsites. Camping areas can be found in a variety settings including shadowy woodlands, sandy shoreline beaches, and secluded islands. A unique opportunity for visitors includes tours through the historic Gillette Castle. This medieval castle is the former home of William Gillette, most famous for his acting role portraying Sherlock Holmes. Aspira has implemented a QR code at the entrance allowing for payment electronically at Gillette Castle and all day-use areas across the state.
Delaware State Parks
Delaware State Parks has progressively expanded their utilization of Aspira's services to include camping reservations, point of sale, ticketing for both tours and waterpark access, passes and permits, and advanced beach access reservations. The partnership notably features an innovative surf fishing permit program implemented in 2023, which uses daily entrance functionality to balance conservation needs with public access through an advanced reservation system. As a 2021 National Gold Medal Award recipient for Excellence in Parks and Recreation Management, Delaware State Parks has achieved significant growth in camping, cabin stays, and overall park attendance throughout their time with Aspira.
Georgia State Parks & Historic Sites
Georgia offers over 2,400 campsites including tent-only areas, RV pull-thru sites, primitive camping, and group camping. Tent/Trailer/RV sites offer electrical and water hook-ups, grills or fire rings, and picnic tables. Aspira partners with Georgia State Parks and Historic Sites to offer a private white label website, reservation systems, and hardware such as desktops, monitors, and receipt printers. Georgia is one of the first states to test out tablets provided by Aspira to sell point of sale items and check-in visitors outside of their visitor centers.
Indiana Department of Natural Resources
Aspira's partnership with Indiana State Parks spans over two decades. With more than 7,000 campsites, 200+ cabins, multiple cottages, group camps, and shelters, Indiana State Parks is one of Aspira's largest camping providers. Aspira helped launch point of sale across the state, totaling more than 140 stations. Indiana Dunes State Parks features three miles of dune lined shores on Lake Michigan and was featured as one of the best places to hike in Indiana by USA Today.
Iowa State Parks
Entering the 15th year of partnership with Aspira, Iowa State Parks offers camping enthusiasts a wide variety of camping opportunities in 55 parks, recreation areas, and state forests. If camping isn't your style, try out a camping cabin, yurt, or family cabin. Aspria provides accommodation and permit solutions, along with credit card terminals for their hardware needs.
Kansas Department of Wildlife and Parks
Kansas has 28 state parks that offer a variety of hiking, camping, wildlife watching, fishing, bike riding, horseback riding, and other activities for visitors. Most offer utility and primitive camping and access to lakes, trails, wildlife areas, and preserved natural areas. Kansas utilizes many of Aspira's flagship features, from gift cards to point of sale. They were the driver behind Aspira's first branded camping app, Campit KS, which allows campers to search for campsites and book directly. Aspira also helps release all of Kansas's inventory through two rush events in mid-December each year.
Kentucky Department of Parks
The Kentucky state park system includes 52 parks and one interstate park with facilities for meetings and conferences, luxury accommodations, camping, golf, education, and more. Kentucky utilizes many of Aspira's offerings, including centralized camping reservations and registrations, point of sale, financial management, marketing services, and support services.
Massachusetts Department of Conservation and Recreation
For over 25 years, Aspira has partnered with Massachusetts to oversee 450,000 acres of the state's parks and forests, beaches, bike trails, watersheds, dams, and parkways. The department also protects land and resources on privately and municipally held land. Aspira provides a commercial, off-the-shelf system for Massachusetts, while ensuring the park system's custom business rules such as minimum stay lengths and resident vs. non-resident fees are automatically calculated and implemented during the booking process.
Montana State Parks
Since 2011, Montana State Parks has worked with Aspira to provide consumer access to their state parks. Over time, Montana has engaged Aspira to support management of camping and day-use reservations for families and groups, marina slip reservations for boaters and anglers, and tour and ticket purchase for Montana State Park attractions.
Nebraska Game and Parks Commission
Nebraska has been one of Aspira's partners since 2007. Nebraska's park system encompasses 86 areas across the state, with popular activities such as boating, hiking, and RV and tent camping. Aspira provides Nebraska’s reservation and point of sale solutions. In 2017, Aspira integrated Nebraska’s Poynt payment processing system with the Aspira One software program.
New Hampshire Division of Parks and Recreation
Collaborating since 2007, Aspira assists New Hampshire State Parks with managing over 73 state parks, campgrounds, historic sites, natural areas, and thousands of miles of trails. New Hampshire takes advantage of a variety of Aspira's features, including check-in software, venue management, ticketing, point of sale, and enhanced insights into occupancy, revenue, and attendance.
New Mexico State Parks
Since 2007, Aspira has helped New Mexico State Parks manage 35 diverse state parks (28 of which have camping facilities) for campers to explore, including cool lakes, mountain forests, canyons, desert beauty, and fascinating historical sites. In 2024, Aspira implemented rental functionality for ADA Trackchair rentals at Manzano Mountains State Park. Since going live with this feature, New Mexico parks leadership have received excellent feedback from visitors for this initiative.
New York State Department of Environmental Conservation & Office of Parks Recreation and Historic Preservation
New York State Parks welcomes millions of visitors each year to enjoy the natural, environmental, historic, and cultural resources of the State. Accommodations offered include campsites, cabins, cottages, yurts, and backcountry camping areas for overnight stays. Aspira provides the solutions to reserve these overnight accommodations, along with day-use reservations such as picnic areas, pavilions, and marinas. Aspira provides the solutions for New York State Parks to operate a customer loyalty program which awards points that can be used toward overnight reservations.
North Carolina State Parks
North Carolina State Parks provides recreational activities to more than 500,000 customers each year and provides access to 36 parks across the state. North Carolina provides lodging, camping, and events to their customers, the latter using a customized version of the system. Aspira partners with North Carolina State Parks to provide connectivity and point of sale access to all their parks and customers.
Oregon Parks and Recreation Department
A partnership that is nearly three decades in the making, Oregon’s state parks are among the most popular in the United States and consistently ranks among the 10 most visited in the nation. Aspira worked with Oregon to move their system away from a mail-in reservation system to a centralized system in the mid-90’s. Today, Oregon serves as one of the leaders in park-technology advancement and adoption.
Pennsylvania State Parks
Aspira partners with Pennsylvania State Parks to provide technology solutions for a wide range of facilities including cabins, yurts, deluxe cottages, and various campsite types, as well as 42 marinas with both transient (float-in) and seasonal slips. Pennsylvania utilizes Aspira's camping, marina, backpacking, and point of sale modules to facilitate unique offerings like river camping with itinerary planning for canoe and kayak enthusiasts.
Rhode Island Department of Environmental Management
Rhode Island offers 9 state park and forestry campgrounds with over 1,000 campsites located within in woodlands, freshwater lakes, and have some located minutes from Rhode Island's beautiful saltwater beaches. The sites range from primitive to developed sites with electric, water, and sewer hookups. In 2023, the state incorporated the Forestry division into Aspira's contract to provide opportunities for visitors to reserve equestrian and backcountry sites.
Texas Parks & Wildlife
Texas Parks & Wildlife Department (TPWD) has partnered with Aspira to enhance their operational capabilities across more than 80 state parks, historic sites, and natural areas. The system enables comprehensive visitor services including campground reservations, day-use bookings, activity reservations, and equipment rentals across Texas's diverse landscapes from desert terrain to pine forests. TPWD pioneered Aspira's innovative kiosk solution, which has served over 50,000 visitors through self-service check-ins and day-use pass purchases. The partnership leverages multiple of Aspira's products including private label website management, point of sale, and marketing to provide a complete park management solution.
Utah State Parks and Recreation
Aspira assists Utah State Parks with managing cabins, cottages, yurts, tiny homes, and more than 2,000 campsites. In 2024, Aspira integrated credit card on file functionality for many site types to help Utah Parks recoup money for any damages caused at their parks.
Private Campgrounds
Firefly Reservations
Firefly Reservations is a cloud-based reservation management solution designed for RV parks and campgrounds. The software lets customers make and pay for reservations online, and allows users to automate a variety of tasks such as sending emails and collecting payments for reservations & utilities.
Firefly Reservations enables the management of short term and long term reservations. Users can create interactive maps of their campground or RV park to display unit availability. Customers can select units and make reservations online through the custom-branded reservation portal, which can be linked to through a button embedded in existing websites. Automated emails allows users to communicate confirmations, reservation information, payment reminders, and other important notices with customers through customizable templates.
Firefly Reservations supports recurring and scheduled payments for monthly guests, storage unit fees, and other regular charges. Utilities can also be recorded and billed through the system, and one-off transactions can be processed through the built-in point of sale (POS). A self-serve kiosk lets customers check themselves in and make payments outside of office hours, and a guest portal for guests to mange their reservation, update payment methods, make payments, and view payment history at any time.
Private Campgrounds and Local Governments
Private Campgrounds and Local Governments provide the customers a number of different camping choices from private agencies across the country.
Other Agencies
Charleston County Park and Recreation Commission
As our campground guest, we invite you to enjoy the natural beauty of James Island County Park, with year-round enjoyment for the entire family. Our 643-acre park offers an abundance of exceptional recreation offerings and natural beauty and is just a short drive from historic downtown Charleston and area beaches.
East Bay Regional Park District, California
Manages 65 parks and 29 regional interpark trails in Alameda and Contra Costa counties.
Estes Valley Recreation and Park District
The Estes Valley Recreation and Park District is a public agency providing park management and recreation programs for members of the community and visitors to Estes Park, Colorado. The District manages 2 campgrounds, 2 golf courses, the marina on Lake Estes, the aquatic center, miles of recreational trails, an indoor and outdoor shooting range, multi-use park facilities that include ball fields, playgrounds, picnic areas, tennis courts, a youth center and a wide variety of recreational programs for all ages. Estes Park has been voted by the Weather Channel as being one of the best Family-Friendly Destinations in the nation and has also been recognized by Trip Advisor with a Traveller's Choice Award as being one of the top 25 destinations in the United States. For more information, please visit www.evrpd.com .
Florida Forest Service
Florida has one of the most extensive and well-managed state forest systems in the nation, with 37 state forests covering 1.1 million acres. Since 2017, Florida Forest Service and Aspira have partnered together to manage more than 80 campgrounds offering primitive to improved campsite experiences. From camping along waterways to hiking meandering trails through the forest, there is something for everyone at Florida’s state forests.
Inyo County Parks and Recreation
Inyo County is a land of fascinating extremes. Here you will find Mt. Whitney, the highest point in the lower 48 states, as well as, Death Valley, the lowest point in North America. Inyo’s seven campgrounds offer dramatic mountain and desert scenery with nearly 400 campsites in close proximity to six million acres of public lands for you to explore. Other natural wonders include the Alabama Hills and the Ancient Bristlecone Pine Forest where you will find the oldest living things on the planet. Activities include; historical sites, hiking, climbing, fishing, off-roading and skiing. Come visit Inyo County on the other side of California.
Kettle Creek Conservation Authority
Thank you for choosing to spend part of your summer with us! A haven for wildlife, and campers alike, the family-friendly conservation areas offer the best of the outdoors in a clean, well-maintained environment. No wonder the majority of our guests are repeat visitors.
Larimer County Department of Natural Resources, Colorado
Campsites, camper cabins, trails, reservoirs (Carter, Flatiron, Horsetooth, Pinewood) from the northern Front Range of the Rockies to Estes Park, Colorado.
NOVA Parks
NOVA Parks campgrounds are situated in two of its largest parks, Bull Run Regional Park in Centreville, VA and Pohick Bay Regional Park in Lorton VA. Each offers space for RV's, campsites with electrical and water hookups, tent sites and cabins. Enjoy all the great park amenities like water access, hiking, swimming and more. All of this while being close to Washington D.C. www.novaparks.com
Oconee County Parks (South Carolina)
Get Outside! Feel Alive! With over 200 campsites and the Mountain Lakes region of South Carolina as your playground, the Outdoors is Yours. South Cove and High Falls park are located along the shores of beautiful Lake Keowee and Chau-Ram park located sits along the Chauga River.
Ohio State Fair
The Ohio State Fair has been a favorite family tradition since 1850! Enjoy a variety of activities and exhibits including interactive educational activities, sporting competitions, a fine arts show, free entertainment stages, a free petting zoo, helicopter rides, a farm animal delivery room, roving performers, agricultural competitions, more than 60 fun rides, horse shows, an 8-acre natural resources park with free kiddie fishing and much more! You won't be able to resist all your favorite Fair goodies from any of the nearly 200 food vendors.
Josephine County Parks, Oregon
Has some of the most beautiful parks in the Pacific Northwest.
All but two camping parks are located on the world famous Rogue
River.
State Camping Highlights
Colorado Camping
Find breathtaking camping in Colorado. Hike, fish, bike, canoe and more at Colorado state parks, forests, and recreation areas. Start you adventure with the perfect campground, cabin, RV park or day use facility.
Georgia Camping
Visit the best Georgia campgrounds. Georgia state parks, forests, beaches and more offer a wide range of activities to help you create the perfect vacation. Check out the best Georgia camping options here.
Indiana Camping
Check out the best of Indiana camping. Located in the heart of the Midwest,
Indiana campgrounds and other facilities within the Indiana DNR offer a get-a-way
destination for Hoosiers and out-of-state visitors alike. Find tent camping and
RV park campgrounds, as well as hidden gems and cabin rentals.
New Hampshire Camping
Check out the best of New Hampshire camping. Find tent camping and RV park
campgrounds, as well as hidden gems and cabin rentals. Here you'll find some of
the best campgrounds and places to camp in New Hampshire.
New Mexico Camping
New Mexico has many diverse State Parks and camping areas to
explore, including cool lakes, mountain forests, canyons, desert
beauty and fascinating historical sites - even dinosaur tracks! Here
you'll find the best campgrounds and places to camp in New Mexico.
North Carolina Camping
North Carolina is blessed with beautiful beaches, majestic
mountains and countless rivers and streams in between. Here you'll
find the best campgrounds and places to camp in North Carolina.
New York Camping
Check out the best of New York camping. From the shores of Long Island to
the mighty Niagara Falls, New York's 179 state parks offer innumerous opportunities
to explore your natural surroundings, escape from the daily grind and discover
exciting new adventures.
Oregon Camping
Enjoy Oregon's 170 state parks and 362 miles of ocean shoreline with amazing cabin and yurt rentals and coastline camping locations.
Pennsylvania Camping
Experience some of the best camping and cabin rentals Pennsylvania has to offer with some top picks for parks to visit on your next Pennsylvania vacation.
Texas Camping
As the largest state in the continental US, Texas offers a broad and diverse expanse of camping opportunities and outdoor activities. Camping in Texas is available year-round in most areas, although we generally recommend your Texas camping trip take place in early Spring or late Fall to avoid hot summer temperatures.

Entiat City Park is the crown jewel of the park system in Entiat. It is located along the west shores of the scenic Columbia River and stretches to the Confluence of the Entiat River. At 40 acres, it is the newest addition to Entiat’s evolving waterfront. Once you arrive, you will find an idyllic peaceful setting to relax or engage in the numerous waterfront activities such as boating, kayaking, SUP, fishing or sunbathing. Or perhaps a walk along the gorgeous ADA accessible trail on the edge of the Columbia River is more to your liking. You will no doubt enjoy the Blue Heron, Bald Eagles, Osprey, and numerous other birds overhead. Don’t forget your lawn chairs, sunscreen, and sporting equipment. The smile will emerge when you pull into our slice of heaven. Early reservations are suggested especially for holiday weekends and peak periods (July and August). For reservations, please contact Camp Spot at Click Here . Prior to making a reservation, please review the Park's Operating Procedures at Click Here and search for Entiat City Park. Park amenities include: 31 RV sites: 29 full-service sites with water, sewer electric (30 &50 amp), picnic tables and fire pits (2 sites available without sewer) 26 designated tent camping sites Restroom facilities with coin-operated showers 2-lane boat launch, dock and truck / trailer parking Picnic shelter (available for rent - see rates below) Playground Equipment RV dump station Many community events are held at this location. Such as: Summerfest – a delightful fun filled day in the sun where there is ample fun for everyone, young and old alike. Summerfest includes food vendors, arts and crafts, and games for the kids. Car shows – offered in the summer featuring hot rods, antique, and collectable treasures for the car enthusiast. Future plans – music festivals Located within 2 miles: Baseball fields Tennis courts and Basketball Courts Café/Restaurants Grocery Store Rates for 2026 Boat Launch Fees Rates 2026 Boat Launch, per boat, per day $5.00 Annual Boat Launch Pass, City Residents $10.00 Annual Boat Launch Pass, Non-City Residents $30.00 Dump Station, Per Visit $5.00 Operating Season Dates and Rates Entiat City Park Regular Operating Season March 16th through November 13th *Senior/Veterans will receive a $10.00 discount per night with proof of age 62 or service identification. CASH FOR CAMPING RESERVATIONS WILL NOT BE ACCEPTED. RESERVATION/CANCELLATION POLICY Refunds of reservations less the reservation fee will be issued when a reservation is canceled up to 7 days prior to the arrival date. Refunds will be issued for cancellations less than 7 days in advance of arrival date less the first night's stay and reservation fee. No Shows will receive no refunds. Refunds for departing from your space before your reservation is over, will not be given. If there are extenuating circumstances (emergency or illness), contact City Hall and fill out a refund request form subject to approval by the mayor. Memorial Day Weekend, 4th of July Weekend, and Labor Day Weekend require a minimum two-night reservation/stay. Complete information, including name, address, phone number, type of camping (tent or RV), and number of people per site, must be submitted at the time of booking. This includes multiple site reservations. Payment may be made with master or visa debit card or credit card. Card payments must be made in full at the time of booking. *Seniors/Veterans will receive a $10.00 discount per night (with proof of age 62 or service identification). The Park & Community Services Advisory Board, established under Entiat Municipal Code Chapter 2.40 , serves as an advisory body to the City Council on matters involving parks, recreation facilities, public use areas, and community services. The Board provides informed recommendations to support planning, development, and stewardship of the City’s recreational and community assets. The Board is composed of five appointed members, selected from residents of the Entiat area who bring local knowledge, sound judgment, and a commitment to community service. City staff and partner agencies may participate in discussions when their expertise is relevant. In accordance with EMC 2.40 , the Board reviews proposals, evaluates community needs, and submits written recommendations to the City Council to guide policy, capital planning, and improvements to public spaces. pages.text:
Campground Directory - ReserveAmerica
Skip to main content
Campground Directory
There are thousands of public and privately-owned campgrounds catering to the needs of millions of campers using tents, travel trailers, motor homes or other types of RVs. Our campground directory will describe each, as to location, season, rates and amenities.
The Followings are the major types of campgrounds:
State Agencies
Colorado Parks and Wildlife
Colorado Parks & Wildlife (CPW) has partnered with Aspira since 1993. In 2018, CPW implemented IPAWS (Integrated Parks and Wildlife System), marking the industry's first fully integrated parks and licensing system. Aspira manages this comprehensive platform that allows users to purchase fishing and hunting licenses, campground reservations, vehicle registrations, hunting reservations, and license draws through a single cart system, serving customers both online and through 400+ license agent locations. A significant enhancement to IPAWS was the 2023 introduction of the Keep Colorado Wild Pass, which integrates with the state's DMV system and has attracted over 2 million participants by offering discounted state park access during vehicle registration renewal.
Connecticut Department of Energy and Environmental Protection
A partner for over 25 years, Connecticut offers campgrounds in thirteen state parks or forests with over 1,400 campsites. Camping areas can be found in a variety settings including shadowy woodlands, sandy shoreline beaches, and secluded islands. A unique opportunity for visitors includes tours through the historic Gillette Castle. This medieval castle is the former home of William Gillette, most famous for his acting role portraying Sherlock Holmes. Aspira has implemented a QR code at the entrance allowing for payment electronically at Gillette Castle and all day-use areas across the state.
Delaware State Parks
Delaware State Parks has progressively expanded their utilization of Aspira's services to include camping reservations, point of sale, ticketing for both tours and waterpark access, passes and permits, and advanced beach access reservations. The partnership notably features an innovative surf fishing permit program implemented in 2023, which uses daily entrance functionality to balance conservation needs with public access through an advanced reservation system. As a 2021 National Gold Medal Award recipient for Excellence in Parks and Recreation Management, Delaware State Parks has achieved significant growth in camping, cabin stays, and overall park attendance throughout their time with Aspira.
Georgia State Parks & Historic Sites
Georgia offers over 2,400 campsites including tent-only areas, RV pull-thru sites, primitive camping, and group camping. Tent/Trailer/RV sites offer electrical and water hook-ups, grills or fire rings, and picnic tables. Aspira partners with Georgia State Parks and Historic Sites to offer a private white label website, reservation systems, and hardware such as desktops, monitors, and receipt printers. Georgia is one of the first states to test out tablets provided by Aspira to sell point of sale items and check-in visitors outside of their visitor centers.
Indiana Department of Natural Resources
Aspira's partnership with Indiana State Parks spans over two decades. With more than 7,000 campsites, 200+ cabins, multiple cottages, group camps, and shelters, Indiana State Parks is one of Aspira's largest camping providers. Aspira helped launch point of sale across the state, totaling more than 140 stations. Indiana Dunes State Parks features three miles of dune lined shores on Lake Michigan and was featured as one of the best places to hike in Indiana by USA Today.
Iowa State Parks
Entering the 15th year of partnership with Aspira, Iowa State Parks offers camping enthusiasts a wide variety of camping opportunities in 55 parks, recreation areas, and state forests. If camping isn't your style, try out a camping cabin, yurt, or family cabin. Aspria provides accommodation and permit solutions, along with credit card terminals for their hardware needs.
Kansas Department of Wildlife and Parks
Kansas has 28 state parks that offer a variety of hiking, camping, wildlife watching, fishing, bike riding, horseback riding, and other activities for visitors. Most offer utility and primitive camping and access to lakes, trails, wildlife areas, and preserved natural areas. Kansas utilizes many of Aspira's flagship features, from gift cards to point of sale. They were the driver behind Aspira's first branded camping app, Campit KS, which allows campers to search for campsites and book directly. Aspira also helps release all of Kansas's inventory through two rush events in mid-December each year.
Kentucky Department of Parks
The Kentucky state park system includes 52 parks and one interstate park with facilities for meetings and conferences, luxury accommodations, camping, golf, education, and more. Kentucky utilizes many of Aspira's offerings, including centralized camping reservations and registrations, point of sale, financial management, marketing services, and support services.
Massachusetts Department of Conservation and Recreation
For over 25 years, Aspira has partnered with Massachusetts to oversee 450,000 acres of the state's parks and forests, beaches, bike trails, watersheds, dams, and parkways. The department also protects land and resources on privately and municipally held land. Aspira provides a commercial, off-the-shelf system for Massachusetts, while ensuring the park system's custom business rules such as minimum stay lengths and resident vs. non-resident fees are automatically calculated and implemented during the booking process.
Montana State Parks
Since 2011, Montana State Parks has worked with Aspira to provide consumer access to their state parks. Over time, Montana has engaged Aspira to support management of camping and day-use reservations for families and groups, marina slip reservations for boaters and anglers, and tour and ticket purchase for Montana State Park attractions.
Nebraska Game and Parks Commission
Nebraska has been one of Aspira's partners since 2007. Nebraska's park system encompasses 86 areas across the state, with popular activities such as boating, hiking, and RV and tent camping. Aspira provides Nebraska’s reservation and point of sale solutions. In 2017, Aspira integrated Nebraska’s Poynt payment processing system with the Aspira One software program.
New Hampshire Division of Parks and Recreation
Collaborating since 2007, Aspira assists New Hampshire State Parks with managing over 73 state parks, campgrounds, historic sites, natural areas, and thousands of miles of trails. New Hampshire takes advantage of a variety of Aspira's features, including check-in software, venue management, ticketing, point of sale, and enhanced insights into occupancy, revenue, and attendance.
New Mexico State Parks
Since 2007, Aspira has helped New Mexico State Parks manage 35 diverse state parks (28 of which have camping facilities) for campers to explore, including cool lakes, mountain forests, canyons, desert beauty, and fascinating historical sites. In 2024, Aspira implemented rental functionality for ADA Trackchair rentals at Manzano Mountains State Park. Since going live with this feature, New Mexico parks leadership have received excellent feedback from visitors for this initiative.
New York State Department of Environmental Conservation & Office of Parks Recreation and Historic Preservation
New York State Parks welcomes millions of visitors each year to enjoy the natural, environmental, historic, and cultural resources of the State. Accommodations offered include campsites, cabins, cottages, yurts, and backcountry camping areas for overnight stays. Aspira provides the solutions to reserve these overnight accommodations, along with day-use reservations such as picnic areas, pavilions, and marinas. Aspira provides the solutions for New York State Parks to operate a customer loyalty program which awards points that can be used toward overnight reservations.
North Carolina State Parks
North Carolina State Parks provides recreational activities to more than 500,000 customers each year and provides access to 36 parks across the state. North Carolina provides lodging, camping, and events to their customers, the latter using a customized version of the system. Aspira partners with North Carolina State Parks to provide connectivity and point of sale access to all their parks and customers.
Oregon Parks and Recreation Department
A partnership that is nearly three decades in the making, Oregon’s state parks are among the most popular in the United States and consistently ranks among the 10 most visited in the nation. Aspira worked with Oregon to move their system away from a mail-in reservation system to a centralized system in the mid-90’s. Today, Oregon serves as one of the leaders in park-technology advancement and adoption.
Pennsylvania State Parks
Aspira partners with Pennsylvania State Parks to provide technology solutions for a wide range of facilities including cabins, yurts, deluxe cottages, and various campsite types, as well as 42 marinas with both transient (float-in) and seasonal slips. Pennsylvania utilizes Aspira's camping, marina, backpacking, and point of sale modules to facilitate unique offerings like river camping with itinerary planning for canoe and kayak enthusiasts.
Rhode Island Department of Environmental Management
Rhode Island offers 9 state park and forestry campgrounds with over 1,000 campsites located within in woodlands, freshwater lakes, and have some located minutes from Rhode Island's beautiful saltwater beaches. The sites range from primitive to developed sites with electric, water, and sewer hookups. In 2023, the state incorporated the Forestry division into Aspira's contract to provide opportunities for visitors to reserve equestrian and backcountry sites.
Texas Parks & Wildlife
Texas Parks & Wildlife Department (TPWD) has partnered with Aspira to enhance their operational capabilities across more than 80 state parks, historic sites, and natural areas. The system enables comprehensive visitor services including campground reservations, day-use bookings, activity reservations, and equipment rentals across Texas's diverse landscapes from desert terrain to pine forests. TPWD pioneered Aspira's innovative kiosk solution, which has served over 50,000 visitors through self-service check-ins and day-use pass purchases. The partnership leverages multiple of Aspira's products including private label website management, point of sale, and marketing to provide a complete park management solution.
Utah State Parks and Recreation
Aspira assists Utah State Parks with managing cabins, cottages, yurts, tiny homes, and more than 2,000 campsites. In 2024, Aspira integrated credit card on file functionality for many site types to help Utah Parks recoup money for any damages caused at their parks.
Private Campgrounds
Firefly Reservations
Firefly Reservations is a cloud-based reservation management solution designed for RV parks and campgrounds. The software lets customers make and pay for reservations online, and allows users to automate a variety of tasks such as sending emails and collecting payments for reservations & utilities.
Firefly Reservations enables the management of short term and long term reservations. Users can create interactive maps of their campground or RV park to display unit availability. Customers can select units and make reservations online through the custom-branded reservation portal, which can be linked to through a button embedded in existing websites. Automated emails allows users to communicate confirmations, reservation information, payment reminders, and other important notices with customers through customizable templates.
Firefly Reservations supports recurring and scheduled payments for monthly guests, storage unit fees, and other regular charges. Utilities can also be recorded and billed through the system, and one-off transactions can be processed through the built-in point of sale (POS). A self-serve kiosk lets customers check themselves in and make payments outside of office hours, and a guest portal for guests to mange their reservation, update payment methods, make payments, and view payment history at any time.
Private Campgrounds and Local Governments
Private Campgrounds and Local Governments provide the customers a number of different camping choices from private agencies across the country.
Other Agencies
Charleston County Park and Recreation Commission
As our campground guest, we invite you to enjoy the natural beauty of James Island County Park, with year-round enjoyment for the entire family. Our 643-acre park offers an abundance of exceptional recreation offerings and natural beauty and is just a short drive from historic downtown Charleston and area beaches.
East Bay Regional Park District, California
Manages 65 parks and 29 regional interpark trails in Alameda and Contra Costa counties.
Estes Valley Recreation and Park District
The Estes Valley Recreation and Park District is a public agency providing park management and recreation programs for members of the community and visitors to Estes Park, Colorado. The District manages 2 campgrounds, 2 golf courses, the marina on Lake Estes, the aquatic center, miles of recreational trails, an indoor and outdoor shooting range, multi-use park facilities that include ball fields, playgrounds, picnic areas, tennis courts, a youth center and a wide variety of recreational programs for all ages. Estes Park has been voted by the Weather Channel as being one of the best Family-Friendly Destinations in the nation and has also been recognized by Trip Advisor with a Traveller's Choice Award as being one of the top 25 destinations in the United States. For more information, please visit www.evrpd.com .
Florida Forest Service
Florida has one of the most extensive and well-managed state forest systems in the nation, with 37 state forests covering 1.1 million acres. Since 2017, Florida Forest Service and Aspira have partnered together to manage more than 80 campgrounds offering primitive to improved campsite experiences. From camping along waterways to hiking meandering trails through the forest, there is something for everyone at Florida’s state forests.
Inyo County Parks and Recreation
Inyo County is a land of fascinating extremes. Here you will find Mt. Whitney, the highest point in the lower 48 states, as well as, Death Valley, the lowest point in North America. Inyo’s seven campgrounds offer dramatic mountain and desert scenery with nearly 400 campsites in close proximity to six million acres of public lands for you to explore. Other natural wonders include the Alabama Hills and the Ancient Bristlecone Pine Forest where you will find the oldest living things on the planet. Activities include; historical sites, hiking, climbing, fishing, off-roading and skiing. Come visit Inyo County on the other side of California.
Kettle Creek Conservation Authority
Thank you for choosing to spend part of your summer with us! A haven for wildlife, and campers alike, the family-friendly conservation areas offer the best of the outdoors in a clean, well-maintained environment. No wonder the majority of our guests are repeat visitors.
Larimer County Department of Natural Resources, Colorado
Campsites, camper cabins, trails, reservoirs (Carter, Flatiron, Horsetooth, Pinewood) from the northern Front Range of the Rockies to Estes Park, Colorado.
NOVA Parks
NOVA Parks campgrounds are situated in two of its largest parks, Bull Run Regional Park in Centreville, VA and Pohick Bay Regional Park in Lorton VA. Each offers space for RV's, campsites with electrical and water hookups, tent sites and cabins. Enjoy all the great park amenities like water access, hiking, swimming and more. All of this while being close to Washington D.C. www.novaparks.com
Oconee County Parks (South Carolina)
Get Outside! Feel Alive! With over 200 campsites and the Mountain Lakes region of South Carolina as your playground, the Outdoors is Yours. South Cove and High Falls park are located along the shores of beautiful Lake Keowee and Chau-Ram park located sits along the Chauga River.
Ohio State Fair
The Ohio State Fair has been a favorite family tradition since 1850! Enjoy a variety of activities and exhibits including interactive educational activities, sporting competitions, a fine arts show, free entertainment stages, a free petting zoo, helicopter rides, a farm animal delivery room, roving performers, agricultural competitions, more than 60 fun rides, horse shows, an 8-acre natural resources park with free kiddie fishing and much more! You won't be able to resist all your favorite Fair goodies from any of the nearly 200 food vendors.
Josephine County Parks, Oregon
Has some of the most beautiful parks in the Pacific Northwest.
All but two camping parks are located on the world famous Rogue
River.
State Camping Highlights
Colorado Camping
Find breathtaking camping in Colorado. Hike, fish, bike, canoe and more at Colorado state parks, forests, and recreation areas. Start you adventure with the perfect campground, cabin, RV park or day use facility.
Georgia Camping
Visit the best Georgia campgrounds. Georgia state parks, forests, beaches and more offer a wide range of activities to help you create the perfect vacation. Check out the best Georgia camping options here.
Indiana Camping
Check out the best of Indiana camping. Located in the heart of the Midwest,
Indiana campgrounds and other facilities within the Indiana DNR offer a get-a-way
destination for Hoosiers and out-of-state visitors alike. Find tent camping and
RV park campgrounds, as well as hidden gems and cabin rentals.
New Hampshire Camping
Check out the best of New Hampshire camping. Find tent camping and RV park
campgrounds, as well as hidden gems and cabin rentals. Here you'll find some of
the best campgrounds and places to camp in New Hampshire.
New Mexico Camping
New Mexico has many diverse State Parks and camping areas to
explore, including cool lakes, mountain forests, canyons, desert
beauty and fascinating historical sites - even dinosaur tracks! Here
you'll find the best campgrounds and places to camp in New Mexico.
North Carolina Camping
North Carolina is blessed with beautiful beaches, majestic
mountains and countless rivers and streams in between. Here you'll
find the best campgrounds and places to camp in North Carolina.
New York Camping
Check out the best of New York camping. From the shores of Long Island to
the mighty Niagara Falls, New York's 179 state parks offer innumerous opportunities
to explore your natural surroundings, escape from the daily grind and discover
exciting new adventures.
Oregon Camping
Enjoy Oregon's 170 state parks and 362 miles of ocean shoreline with amazing cabin and yurt rentals and coastline camping locations.
Pennsylvania Camping
Experience some of the best camping and cabin rentals Pennsylvania has to offer with some top picks for parks to visit on your next Pennsylvania vacation.
Texas Camping
As the largest state in the continental US, Texas offers a broad and diverse expanse of camping opportunities and outdoor activities. Camping in Texas is available year-round in most areas, although we generally recommend your Texas camping trip take place in early Spring or late Fall to avoid hot summer temperatures.

Camp Wilkerson
Home
> Departments
> Parks, Forests, and Recreation
> Camp Wilkerson
Camp Wilkerson is considered one of the Columbia County’s most quiet and secluded areas. At 280 acres, it is the county’s largest park, with more than 13 miles of trails for hikers and horseback riders.
The heavily-wood Camp Wilkerson offers a horse camp, 24 three-sided camp shelters referred to as Adirondack camps, 23 sites, 2 dry RV sites, three rustic two-room cabins and a day lodge complete with cooking facilities to accommodate groups of up to 250 people. All camping sites include a picnic table and fire ring.
Remote pathways and roads lead through the park’s dense evergreen and hardwood temperate forest. Trail users can travel on either forest roads or the single-track 3.5 mile Liahona Trail that loops through the park and crosses bridges over Oak Ranch Creek. Wider forest roads bring riders on five, seven or 10-mile loops through the thick forest. All trails are considered easy to moderate.
Camp Wilkerson is located 16 miles northwest of Scappoose on Apiary Road. It is open year round, except for the lodge, which is closed during winter months.

Home
> Departments

> Hudson Parcher Park
Hudson Parcher Park is a hidden gem deep in the forested hills of Columbia County. A quiet place to camp or relax for a day, the park lies about four miles from Rainier, Oregon, and is traversed by Beaver Creek. Visitors can enjoy tent or RV camping, hiking, cycling, fishing, canoeing and birding. Hudson Parcher has 10 tent sites, 25 RV sites, a bike camping site, playgrounds for the kids, picnic tables, fire rings, volleyball courts, baseball fields, flushing toilets and hot showers. Camp hosts staff the park in the summer months. This beautiful spot is perfect for events as there is a day use lodge with a kitchen available too.
Located in the county's deep temperate forest, Hudson Parcher is covered with older, second-growth forest. Douglas firs and big leaf maple offer shade while ferns, Oregon grape and other native plants provide undercover. Beaver Creek meanders through the 27-acre park, offering the opportunity to fish or catch crawdads.

Camp Wilkerson
Home
> Departments
> Parks, Forests, and Recreation
> Camp Wilkerson
Camp Wilkerson is considered one of the Columbia County’s most quiet and secluded areas. At 280 acres, it is the county’s largest park, with more than 13 miles of trails for hikers and horseback riders.
The heavily-wood Camp Wilkerson offers a horse camp, 24 three-sided camp shelters referred to as Adirondack camps, 23 sites, 2 dry RV sites, three rustic two-room cabins and a day lodge complete with cooking facilities to accommodate groups of up to 250 people. All camping sites include a picnic table and fire ring.
Remote pathways and roads lead through the park’s dense evergreen and hardwood temperate forest. Trail users can travel on either forest roads or the single-track 3.5 mile Liahona Trail that loops through the park and crosses bridges over Oak Ranch Creek. Wider forest roads bring riders on five, seven or 10-mile loops through the thick forest. All trails are considered easy to moderate.
Camp Wilkerson is located 16 miles northwest of Scappoose on Apiary Road. It is open year round, except for the lodge, which is closed during winter months.

pages.title: Campground Directory - ReserveAmerica
pages.text:
Campground Directory - ReserveAmerica
Skip to main content
Campground Directory
There are thousands of public and privately-owned campgrounds catering to the needs of millions of campers using tents, travel trailers, motor homes or other types of RVs. Our campground directory will describe each, as to location, season, rates and amenities.
The Followings are the major types of campgrounds:
State Agencies
Colorado Parks and Wildlife
Colorado Parks & Wildlife (CPW) has partnered with Aspira since 1993. In 2018, CPW implemented IPAWS (Integrated Parks and Wildlife System), marking the industry's first fully integrated parks and licensing system. Aspira manages this comprehensive platform that allows users to purchase fishing and hunting licenses, campground reservations, vehicle registrations, hunting reservations, and license draws through a single cart system, serving customers both online and through 400+ license agent locations. A significant enhancement to IPAWS was the 2023 introduction of the Keep Colorado Wild Pass, which integrates with the state's DMV system and has attracted over 2 million participants by offering discounted state park access during vehicle registration renewal.
Connecticut Department of Energy and Environmental Protection
A partner for over 25 years, Connecticut offers campgrounds in thirteen state parks or forests with over 1,400 campsites. Camping areas can be found in a variety settings including shadowy woodlands, sandy shoreline beaches, and secluded islands. A unique opportunity for visitors includes tours through the historic Gillette Castle. This medieval castle is the former home of William Gillette, most famous for his acting role portraying Sherlock Holmes. Aspira has implemented a QR code at the entrance allowing for payment electronically at Gillette Castle and all day-use areas across the state.
Delaware State Parks
Delaware State Parks has progressively expanded their utilization of Aspira's services to include camping reservations, point of sale, ticketing for both tours and waterpark access, passes and permits, and advanced beach access reservations. The partnership notably features an innovative surf fishing permit program implemented in 2023, which uses daily entrance functionality to balance conservation needs with public access through an advanced reservation system. As a 2021 National Gold Medal Award recipient for Excellence in Parks and Recreation Management, Delaware State Parks has achieved significant growth in camping, cabin stays, and overall park attendance throughout their time with Aspira.
Georgia State Parks & Historic Sites
Georgia offers over 2,400 campsites including tent-only areas, RV pull-thru sites, primitive camping, and group camping. Tent/Trailer/RV sites offer electrical and water hook-ups, grills or fire rings, and picnic tables. Aspira partners with Georgia State Parks and Historic Sites to offer a private white label website, reservation systems, and hardware such as desktops, monitors, and receipt printers. Georgia is one of the first states to test out tablets provided by Aspira to sell point of sale items and check-in visitors outside of their visitor centers.
Indiana Department of Natural Resources
Aspira's partnership with Indiana State Parks spans over two decades. With more than 7,000 campsites, 200+ cabins, multiple cottages, group camps, and shelters, Indiana State Parks is one of Aspira's largest camping providers. Aspira helped launch point of sale across the state, totaling more than 140 stations. Indiana Dunes State Parks features three miles of dune lined shores on Lake Michigan and was featured as one of the best places to hike in Indiana by USA Today.
Iowa State Parks
Entering the 15th year of partnership with Aspira, Iowa State Parks offers camping enthusiasts a wide variety of camping opportunities in 55 parks, recreation areas, and state forests. If camping isn't your style, try out a camping cabin, yurt, or family cabin. Aspria provides accommodation and permit solutions, along with credit card terminals for their hardware needs.
Kansas Department of Wildlife and Parks
Kansas has 28 state parks that offer a variety of hiking, camping, wildlife watching, fishing, bike riding, horseback riding, and other activities for visitors. Most offer utility and primitive camping and access to lakes, trails, wildlife areas, and preserved natural areas. Kansas utilizes many of Aspira's flagship features, from gift cards to point of sale. They were the driver behind Aspira's first branded camping app, Campit KS, which allows campers to search for campsites and book directly. Aspira also helps release all of Kansas's inventory through two rush events in mid-December each year.
Kentucky Department of Parks
The Kentucky state park system includes 52 parks and one interstate park with facilities for meetings and conferences, luxury accommodations, camping, golf, education, and more. Kentucky utilizes many of Aspira's offerings, including centralized camping reservations and registrations, point of sale, financial management, marketing services, and support services.
Massachusetts Department of Conservation and Recreation
For over 25 years, Aspira has partnered with Massachusetts to oversee 450,000 acres of the state's parks and forests, beaches, bike trails, watersheds, dams, and parkways. The department also protects land and resources on privately and municipally held land. Aspira provides a commercial, off-the-shelf system for Massachusetts, while ensuring the park system's custom business rules such as minimum stay lengths and resident vs. non-resident fees are automatically calculated and implemented during the booking process.
Montana State Parks
Since 2011, Montana State Parks has worked with Aspira to provide consumer access to their state parks. Over time, Montana has engaged Aspira to support management of camping and day-use reservations for families and groups, marina slip reservations for boaters and anglers, and tour and ticket purchase for Montana State Park attractions.
Nebraska Game and Parks Commission
Nebraska has been one of Aspira's partners since 2007. Nebraska's park system encompasses 86 areas across the state, with popular activities such as boating, hiking, and RV and tent camping. Aspira provides Nebraska’s reservation and point of sale solutions. In 2017, Aspira integrated Nebraska’s Poynt payment processing system with the Aspira One software program.
New Hampshire Division of Parks and Recreation
Collaborating since 2007, Aspira assists New Hampshire State Parks with managing over 73 state parks, campgrounds, historic sites, natural areas, and thousands of miles of trails. New Hampshire takes advantage of a variety of Aspira's features, including check-in software, venue management, ticketing, point of sale, and enhanced insights into occupancy, revenue, and attendance.
New Mexico State Parks
Since 2007, Aspira has helped New Mexico State Parks manage 35 diverse state parks (28 of which have camping facilities) for campers to explore, including cool lakes, mountain forests, canyons, desert beauty, and fascinating historical sites. In 2024, Aspira implemented rental functionality for ADA Trackchair rentals at Manzano Mountains State Park. Since going live with this feature, New Mexico parks leadership have received excellent feedback from visitors for this initiative.
New York State Department of Environmental Conservation & Office of Parks Recreation and Historic Preservation
New York State Parks welcomes millions of visitors each year to enjoy the natural, environmental, historic, and cultural resources of the State. Accommodations offered include campsites, cabins, cottages, yurts, and backcountry camping areas for overnight stays. Aspira provides the solutions to reserve these overnight accommodations, along with day-use reservations such as picnic areas, pavilions, and marinas. Aspira provides the solutions for New York State Parks to operate a customer loyalty program which awards points that can be used toward overnight reservations.
North Carolina State Parks
North Carolina State Parks provides recreational activities to more than 500,000 customers each year and provides access to 36 parks across the state. North Carolina provides lodging, camping, and events to their customers, the latter using a customized version of the system. Aspira partners with North Carolina State Parks to provide connectivity and point of sale access to all their parks and customers.
Oregon Parks and Recreation Department
A partnership that is nearly three decades in the making, Oregon’s state parks are among the most popular in the United States and consistently ranks among the 10 most visited in the nation. Aspira worked with Oregon to move their system away from a mail-in reservation system to a centralized system in the mid-90’s. Today, Oregon serves as one of the leaders in park-technology advancement and adoption.
Pennsylvania State Parks
Aspira partners with Pennsylvania State Parks to provide technology solutions for a wide range of facilities including cabins, yurts, deluxe cottages, and various campsite types, as well as 42 marinas with both transient (float-in) and seasonal slips. Pennsylvania utilizes Aspira's camping, marina, backpacking, and point of sale modules to facilitate unique offerings like river camping with itinerary planning for canoe and kayak enthusiasts.
Rhode Island Department of Environmental Management
Rhode Island offers 9 state park and forestry campgrounds with over 1,000 campsites located within in woodlands, freshwater lakes, and have some located minutes from Rhode Island's beautiful saltwater beaches. The sites range from primitive to developed sites with electric, water, and sewer hookups. In 2023, the state incorporated the Forestry division into Aspira's contract to provide opportunities for visitors to reserve equestrian and backcountry sites.
Texas Parks & Wildlife
Texas Parks & Wildlife Department (TPWD) has partnered with Aspira to enhance their operational capabilities across more than 80 state parks, historic sites, and natural areas. The system enables comprehensive visitor services including campground reservations, day-use bookings, activity reservations, and equipment rentals across Texas's diverse landscapes from desert terrain to pine forests. TPWD pioneered Aspira's innovative kiosk solution, which has served over 50,000 visitors through self-service check-ins and day-use pass purchases. The partnership leverages multiple of Aspira's products including private label website management, point of sale, and marketing to provide a complete park management solution.
Utah State Parks and Recreation
Aspira assists Utah State Parks with managing cabins, cottages, yurts, tiny homes, and more than 2,000 campsites. In 2024, Aspira integrated credit card on file functionality for many site types to help Utah Parks recoup money for any damages caused at their parks.
Private Campgrounds
Firefly Reservations
Firefly Reservations is a cloud-based reservation management solution designed for RV parks and campgrounds. The software lets customers make and pay for reservations online, and allows users to automate a variety of tasks such as sending emails and collecting payments for reservations & utilities.
Firefly Reservations enables the management of short term and long term reservations. Users can create interactive maps of their campground or RV park to display unit availability. Customers can select units and make reservations online through the custom-branded reservation portal, which can be linked to through a button embedded in existing websites. Automated emails allows users to communicate confirmations, reservation information, payment reminders, and other important notices with customers through customizable templates.
Firefly Reservations supports recurring and scheduled payments for monthly guests, storage unit fees, and other regular charges. Utilities can also be recorded and billed through the system, and one-off transactions can be processed through the built-in point of sale (POS). A self-serve kiosk lets customers check themselves in and make payments outside of office hours, and a guest portal for guests to mange their reservation, update payment methods, make payments, and view payment history at any time.
Private Campgrounds and Local Governments
Private Campgrounds and Local Governments provide the customers a number of different camping choices from private agencies across the country.
Other Agencies
Charleston County Park and Recreation Commission
As our campground guest, we invite you to enjoy the natural beauty of James Island County Park, with year-round enjoyment for the entire family. Our 643-acre park offers an abundance of exceptional recreation offerings and natural beauty and is just a short drive from historic downtown Charleston and area beaches.
East Bay Regional Park District, California
Manages 65 parks and 29 regional interpark trails in Alameda and Contra Costa counties.
Estes Valley Recreation and Park District
The Estes Valley Recreation and Park District is a public agency providing park management and recreation programs for members of the community and visitors to Estes Park, Colorado. The District manages 2 campgrounds, 2 golf courses, the marina on Lake Estes, the aquatic center, miles of recreational trails, an indoor and outdoor shooting range, multi-use park facilities that include ball fields, playgrounds, picnic areas, tennis courts, a youth center and a wide variety of recreational programs for all ages. Estes Park has been voted by the Weather Channel as being one of the best Family-Friendly Destinations in the nation and has also been recognized by Trip Advisor with a Traveller's Choice Award as being one of the top 25 destinations in the United States. For more information, please visit www.evrpd.com .
Florida Forest Service
Florida has one of the most extensive and well-managed state forest systems in the nation, with 37 state forests covering 1.1 million acres. Since 2017, Florida Forest Service and Aspira have partnered together to manage more than 80 campgrounds offering primitive to improved campsite experiences. From camping along waterways to hiking meandering trails through the forest, there is something for everyone at Florida’s state forests.
Inyo County Parks and Recreation
Inyo County is a land of fascinating extremes. Here you will find Mt. Whitney, the highest point in the lower 48 states, as well as, Death Valley, the lowest point in North America. Inyo’s seven campgrounds offer dramatic mountain and desert scenery with nearly 400 campsites in close proximity to six million acres of public lands for you to explore. Other natural wonders include the Alabama Hills and the Ancient Bristlecone Pine Forest where you will find the oldest living things on the planet. Activities include; historical sites, hiking, climbing, fishing, off-roading and skiing. Come visit Inyo County on the other side of California.
Kettle Creek Conservation Authority
Thank you for choosing to spend part of your summer with us! A haven for wildlife, and campers alike, the family-friendly conservation areas offer the best of the outdoors in a clean, well-maintained environment. No wonder the majority of our guests are repeat visitors.
Larimer County Department of Natural Resources, Colorado
Campsites, camper cabins, trails, reservoirs (Carter, Flatiron, Horsetooth, Pinewood) from the northern Front Range of the Rockies to Estes Park, Colorado.
NOVA Parks
NOVA Parks campgrounds are situated in two of its largest parks, Bull Run Regional Park in Centreville, VA and Pohick Bay Regional Park in Lorton VA. Each offers space for RV's, campsites with electrical and water hookups, tent sites and cabins. Enjoy all the great park amenities like water access, hiking, swimming and more. All of this while being close to Washington D.C. www.novaparks.com
Oconee County Parks (South Carolina)
Get Outside! Feel Alive! With over 200 campsites and the Mountain Lakes region of South Carolina as your playground, the Outdoors is Yours. South Cove and High Falls park are located along the shores of beautiful Lake Keowee and Chau-Ram park located sits along the Chauga River.
Ohio State Fair
The Ohio State Fair has been a favorite family tradition since 1850! Enjoy a variety of activities and exhibits including interactive educational activities, sporting competitions, a fine arts show, free entertainment stages, a free petting zoo, helicopter rides, a farm animal delivery room, roving performers, agricultural competitions, more than 60 fun rides, horse shows, an 8-acre natural resources park with free kiddie fishing and much more! You won't be able to resist all your favorite Fair goodies from any of the nearly 200 food vendors.
Josephine County Parks, Oregon
Has some of the most beautiful parks in the Pacific Northwest.
All but two camping parks are located on the world famous Rogue
River.
State Camping Highlights
Colorado Camping
Find breathtaking camping in Colorado. Hike, fish, bike, canoe and more at Colorado state parks, forests, and recreation areas. Start you adventure with the perfect campground, cabin, RV park or day use facility.
Georgia Camping
Visit the best Georgia campgrounds. Georgia state parks, forests, beaches and more offer a wide range of activities to help you create the perfect vacation. Check out the best Georgia camping options here.
Indiana Camping
Check out the best of Indiana camping. Located in the heart of the Midwest,
Indiana campgrounds and other facilities within the Indiana DNR offer a get-a-way
destination for Hoosiers and out-of-state visitors alike. Find tent camping and
RV park campgrounds, as well as hidden gems and cabin rentals.
New Hampshire Camping
Check out the best of New Hampshire camping. Find tent camping and RV park
campgrounds, as well as hidden gems and cabin rentals. Here you'll find some of
the best campgrounds and places to camp in New Hampshire.
New Mexico Camping
New Mexico has many diverse State Parks and camping areas to
explore, including cool lakes, mountain forests, canyons, desert
beauty and fascinating historical sites - even dinosaur tracks! Here
you'll find the best campgrounds and places to camp in New Mexico.
North Carolina Camping
North Carolina is blessed with beautiful beaches, majestic
mountains and countless rivers and streams in between. Here you'll
find the best campgrounds and places to camp in North Carolina.
New York Camping
Check out the best of New York camping. From the shores of Long Island to
the mighty Niagara Falls, New York's 179 state parks offer innumerous opportunities
to explore your natural surroundings, escape from the daily grind and discover
exciting new adventures.
Oregon Camping
Enjoy Oregon's 170 state parks and 362 miles of ocean shoreline with amazing cabin and yurt rentals and coastline camping locations.
Pennsylvania Camping
Experience some of the best camping and cabin rentals Pennsylvania has to offer with some top picks for parks to visit on your next Pennsylvania vacation.
Texas Camping
As the largest state in the continental US, Texas offers a broad and diverse expanse of camping opportunities and outdoor activities. Camping in Texas is available year-round in most areas, although we generally recommend your Texas camping trip take place in early Spring or late Fall to avoid hot summer temperatures.

Anthony Chabot Family Campground Closure
Anthony Chabot Family Campground will be closed Oct. 12, 2026 - Nov. 30, 2026, for restroom improvements and hazardous tree work. Campsites and the RV Sewage Disposal Station in this area will be inaccessible until Dec. 1, 2026.
Anthony Chabot Campground sits approximately 1 ½ miles above Lake Chabot in Castro Valley, California. The campground has 75 campsites which include: 12 RV sites with full-hookups (30 amp), 1 developed group site, 53 drive-up tent sites, and 10 hike-in tent sites. Hike-In Tent sites (#13-22) are NOT backpack sites; they are inside the campground but without vehicle access nor adjacent parking. Parking pads average 30 feet; the largest is 39 feet. The campground also has hot showers, flush toilets, seasonal campfire programs, an amphitheater, and a dump station (additional use fees may apply).
In addition to the main campground, there are also 6 primitive group campsites. A minimum of 17 people are required to reserve a group campsite and maximum capacity varies from 35 to 300. Primitive group campsites are not inside the campground and are located behind the group camp gate. Primitive group campsites have no access to showers or flush toilets. Group campsites have picnic table(s), fire ring with grill, water, and chemical/vault toilets. RV’s, trailers, motorhomes, etc. are not permitted at the group campsites.
Campground gates are locked between the hours of 10pm to 8am. Plan arrival times and excursions accordingly. Generators and smoking are prohibited. No camp store. Dogs are allowed, leashed, and attended to at all times.

Heritage / Special Months
The Park District and the Regional Parks Foundation celebrate the diverse communities in the East Bay.
Diversity encompasses race, ethnic origin, socio-economic background, religion, sexual orientation, age and ability, to name but a few. Underlying the broad spectrum of diversity is our shared humanity with aspirations and needs to be seen, heard, included, and celebrated.

Group Campsites

Recreation

Camping

Group Campsites
Back to top
Group campsites offer the opportunity for groups of 10 or more (site capacity minimums and maximums vary) to camp together in one large site. Group campsites are either developed (inside family campgrounds) and have access to flush toilets and showers, or primitive (no showers or flush toilets; chemical toilets on-site). Some group campsites have parking near the site, and others are hike-in only.
The information below may change at any time. Fires are only allowed in designated fire rings, and may not be allowed if restrictions are in place. You will need to check the Fire Danger Levels and Restrictions page for more information. Water may also be unavailable, and is unreliable at some parks, you should always plan to bring in your own drinking water.
Group campsites are available at:
Anthony Chabot Regional Park
Black Diamond Mines Regional Preserve
Briones Regional Park
Coyote Hills Regional Park
Del Valle Regional Park
Garin Regional Park
Las Trampas Wilderness Regional Preserve
Point Pinole Regional Shoreline
Reinhardt Redwood Regional Park
Tilden Regional Park
