Reservations:
Camping in the park requires a reservation. Family campground sites must be reserved 2 or more business days in advance. Group campsites must be reserved 3 or more business days in advance.
Check availability at ReserveAmerica.com
(opens external link in a new window) for Family, Group, and Equestrian (Horse) Campsites. Search by park name. Family Campsite reservations can also be made online at Reserve America.
ADA campsites, and group campsites must be reserved by phone only by calling Reservations:
1 (888) 327-2757 , option 2: Mon.- Fri. 9am-4pm.
For persons with hearing impairments, please use the Telecommunications Relay Service at 711. *For Canadian residents, please use 510-544-2707 .
Group Campsites
Wild Turkey (Developed/ 17-50 person capacity)
• Site closed seasonally November 1 – March 31
The site is located within the family campground and includes picnic tables, BBQ, fire ring, and drinking fountain/water spigot. Access to flush toilets and showers, nearby within the family campground. Beer and wine are permitted, no hard alcohol. 15 parking passes issued with reservation. Buses, RVs, trailers, food trucks, or caterers are prohibited.
Image
Image
Image
Punta Vaca (Developed/ 17 - 50 person capacity)
Site closed seasonally November 1 – March 31
This site is located within the family campground and includes picnic tables, BBQ, fire ring, a drinking fountain with spigot and chemical toilets. Flush toilets and showers are located nearby in the family campground. Beer and wine is permitted, no hard alcohol. 15 parking passes issued with reservation. Buses, RVs, trailers, food trucks, or caterers are prohibited.
Cedar Camp (Primitive/ 17 - 50 person capacity)
Closed until further notice
Site closed seasonally November 1 – March 31
Cedar Camp is a primitive site with partial shade and includes picnic tables, BBQ, a fire circle with benches, and two chemical toilets. There is a 1/4 mile hike in to the site and you must hike in all of your gear. Water is not available at the site, you must bring in your drinking water. No access to showers. Beer and wine is permitted with additional $25 Beer and Wine Permit. 10 parking passes issued with reservation. Buses, RVs, trailers, food trucks, or caterers are prohibited.
Image
Image
Image
Ardilla (Primitive/ 17 - 50 person capacity)
This is a primitive campsite with picnic tables, BBQ, a fire circle with benches, and a water spigot. There is no access to showers and flush toilets are located near the site. Beer and wine is permitted with additional $25 Beer and Wine Permit. 10 parking passes issued with reservation. Buses, RVs, trailers, food trucks, or caterers are prohibited.
Image
Image
Image
Eagles View (Primitive/ 17- 50 person capacity)
This site has a view of the lake and includes picnic tables, BBQs, fire ring, and a drinking fountain. Flush toilets are available uphill from the site an there is no access to showers. Beer and wine is permitted with additional $25 Beer and Wine Permit. 10 parking passes issued with reservation. Buses, RVs, trailers, food trucks, or caterers are prohibited.
Image
Image
Image
Venados (Primitive/ 17- 50 person capacity)
Site closed seasonally November 1 – March 31
Venados is a primitive campsite located near the lake and includes three 10' tables, one serving table, one XL BBQ, a fire circle with benches. Two pit toilets (ADA) with fans are available at the site. There is no access to showers. There is no water at the site, a water spigot is located near Hetch Hetchy. Beer and wine is permitted with additional $25 Beer and Wine Permit. 10 parking passes issued with reservation. Buses, RVs, trailers, food trucks, or caterers are prohibited.
Hetch Hetchy (Primitive/ 50-100 capacity)
Site closed seasonally November 1 – March 31
Hetch Hetchy is a primitive campsite located near the lake and includes two 6' tables, a serving table, a XL BBQ, a fire circle with seating, and a water spigot. Three pit toilets (ADA) with fans are available at the site; there is no access to showers. Boats can be anchored or launched from site. Beer and wine is permitted with additional $25 Beer and Wine Permit. 20 parking passes issued with reservation. Buses, RVs, trailers, food trucks, or caterers are prohibited.
Equestrian Campsites
Little Chaparral (1 - 4 person capacity/per site)
Little Chaparral has 4 campsites which can accommodate up to 4 people maximum at each. A household can reserve up to 4 sites. Horse paddock is 10’ X 10’ and each site accommodates 1 horse maximum. 1 truck and 1 trailer can park at each site and there is no additional vehicles permitted. There is no fire circle at the site. Water, flush toilets, and showers are available in the family campground. Water at site is for horses only, not for human consumption. Bring your own feed.
Caballo Loco (Primitive Group/ 4 – 50 person capacity)
Site closed seasonally November 1 – March 31
Caballo Loco is an equestrian group site that can accommodate up to 15 horses; 5 horses is the minimum to reserve. This site includes picnic tables, BBQs, a three pole tethering system (requires 100' rope), fifteen horse paddocks (one horse max per paddock), a manure bin, a dumpster and shovel, a fire circle with benches, a small covered shelter, and a chemical toilet. Non-potable water is available at site for horses but it is not for human consumption. You must bring in your own drinking water; no access to showers or flush toilets. You must bring your own feed. Vehicles and tents must stay inside the fenced area. The dumpster needs to remain clear and accessible. Beer and wine is permitted with additional $25 Beer and Wine Permit. No hard alcohol. 10 parking passes issued with reservation, which includes trailers.

Heritage / Special Months
The Park District and the Regional Parks Foundation celebrate the diverse communities in the East Bay.
Diversity encompasses race, ethnic origin, socio-economic background, religion, sexual orientation, age and ability, to name but a few. Underlying the broad spectrum of diversity is our shared humanity with aspirations and needs to be seen, heard, included, and celebrated.

Submit your request by filling out the Special Interest Months and Observances Requests Form. Requests for one-time Observances should be made with as much advance notice as possible, with a minimum of 3 months' notice. Requests for annual Observances should be submitted before July 31 of the preceding year for priority consideration.

Recreation

Camping

Group Campsites
Back to top
Group campsites offer the opportunity for groups of 10 or more (site capacity minimums and maximums vary) to camp together in one large site. Group campsites are either developed (inside family campgrounds) and have access to flush toilets and showers, or primitive (no showers or flush toilets; chemical toilets on-site). Some group campsites have parking near the site, and others are hike-in only.
The information below may change at any time. Fires are only allowed in designated fire rings, and may not be allowed if restrictions are in place. You will need to check the Fire Danger Levels and Restrictions page for more information. Water may also be unavailable, and is unreliable at some parks, you should always plan to bring in your own drinking water.
Group campsites are available at:
Anthony Chabot Regional Park
Black Diamond Mines Regional Preserve
Briones Regional Park
Coyote Hills Regional Park
Del Valle Regional Park
Garin Regional Park
Las Trampas Wilderness Regional Preserve
Point Pinole Regional Shoreline
Reinhardt Redwood Regional Park
Tilden Regional Park

Reservations:
Group campsite reservations must be made at least 3 business days prior to your arrival date.
(Example: The last day to reserve for a Friday arrival date is the previous Tuesday.)
Booking Window: Sites are released in 2 Six-month block release windows. Maximum 2 reservations per call.
Group and Backpacking reservations with arrival dates from July through December 2026 are now open.
For Group and Backpacking campsites with arrival dates from January through June 2027, sites will be open for Reservations in December 2026.

How to Make Coffee While Camping
How to Make Coffee While Camping
Relaxing at your campsite and sipping your morning coffee as the day begins is a treasured moment on any camping trip. There are plenty of ways to learn how to make coffee while camping and we have highlighted five sure-fire favorites below.
Recommended: Camping Breakfast Ideas
1. Percolator Camping Coffee
If the question is how to make coffee while camping like grandma did? – then percolator coffee is surely the answer. This style of coffee requires a percolator coffee pot, which looks like a kettle and includes a press and filter inside. The result is a robust, if not sometimes bitter coffee, with the grinds completely separated from the water.
Fill the bottom chamber with cold water and the basket with coarse coffee grinds – about 1.5 tablespoons per cup of water
Secure the top of the percolator and put on a heat source set at about medium-high heat.
Bring to a boil and simmer for ten minutes.
Pour your cup of Joe.
Recommended: Great Summer RV Trips for Families
2. Pre-Packaged/Steeped Camping Coffee
When it is time to level up on the coffee flavor, while also minimizing the items you need to make coffee while camping, then steeped coffee is the way to go. You read that right. This coffee comes in a pouch and is brewed much like how you would steep an individual tea bag. Wildland Coffee is leading the way in the easy-to-make and tasty campsite coffee revolution, and Apex Club members get a discount. This method is great for any camping situation, and especially so for backpackers or those camping light on equipment.
To make steeped coffee simply:
Heat 8 ounces of water to almost a boil.
Add a bag of coffee and steep for eight minutes.
Remove the bag and sip away!
3. French Press Camping Coffee
French press coffee delivers fantastic flavor when done right. The trick is using medium ground grinds. Too fine a grind and you will end up with a muddy mess. Too coarse a grind and you will lose out on flavor. You can bring the tried-and-true glass french press but keep in mind that it is delicate and may not be durable enough for your camping trip. A plastic French press may be a better option for making coffee while camping, although in either case, a French press does take up some room and is not ideal for campers who need to go light with their equipment.
How to make coffee while camping with a French press coffee requires:
Heat water to a near boil.
Remove the plunger and add medium ground coffee to the chamber, about 1.5 tablespoons per cup of water.
Pour water into the chamber and stir grinds in water for about 10 seconds.
Insert the plunger and press down so it rests just above the water.
Let the coffee brew for about 4 minutes.
Slowly push down on the plunger until it reaches the bottom of the chamber.
Pour and enjoy
Recommended: Campgrounds with Boat Launches Across the US
4. AeroPress Camping Coffee
An AeroPress makes consistently outstanding coffee and is a favorite coffee-making contraption among coffee lovers. An AeroPress consists of a few relatively small plastic pieces, and a paper or mesh reusable filter. With its straightforward useability and packability, an AeroPress works well for many camping situations (although not backpacking). One drawback with an AeroPress is that you can only make one cup of Joe at a time.
How to make coffee while camping with an AeroPress, simply:
Heat water to a near boil.
Insert the filter in basket and twist basket onto the brew chamber.
Place the brew chamber with the basket over your mug.
Add finely-ground coffee into the chamber (about 1.5 tablespoons per cup).
Fill the chamber with hot water.
Stir the water and grounds for about 10 seconds.
Insert the plunger and leave at the top. Let coffee brew for about 1 minute.
Press plunger down so coffee comes directly into the mug.
5. Cowboy Coffee
This is the classic, traditional way to make backcountry coffee. While you’ll get points for the ruggedness factor of cowboy coffee, the acrid taste, and remnant grinds may not be preferred for some.
To make cowboy coffee:
Bring water to a boil in a kettle.
Add coarsely-ground coffee grinds, one tablespoon per 1.5 cups of water.
Stir the grinds and let the kettle boil for two minutes.
Remove the kettle from heat.
Remove the grinds by skimming the top of the water, or adding about 1oz of cold water and waiting a minute for the grinds to settle. (In the olden days, cowboys would also add eggshells to the kettle to keep the grounds down and enhance the flavor.)
Pour your cup and enjoy!
Are you ready for your adventure? Plan your camping trip!

Welcome to Inyo County Parks & Recreation!
Reservations for all Inyo County campgrounds can be made at ReserveAmerica.com .
Inyo County Parks & Recreation is proud to offer and maintain fifteen beautiful parks and campgrounds for both residents and visitors. Each county-operated campground features a flowing creek in a rustic setting, creating a memorable outdoor experience.
Several of our lower-elevation campgrounds provide excellent fishing opportunities, with creeks regularly stocked with trout during the season—all conveniently located along U.S. Highway 395.
Independence Creek Campground sites 16–29 are closed until further notice due to a damaged bridge that provides access to this area. For the safety of all visitors, these sites will remain inaccessible while repairs are underway.
We appreciate your patience and understanding, and we will provide updates as soon as more information becomes available.
For questions or alternative site availability, please contact the campground office.
Pleasant Valley Campground offers year-round fishing in the Owens River.
Diaz Lake Campground features an 80-acre lake ideal for fishing, boating, and water sports. Shore fishing is open year-round, and a valid CA fishing license is required.
The Millpond Recreation Area spans over 120 acres and offers a wide variety of amenities, including:
A new disc golf course
Tennis courts
Play equipment
A gazebo for special events
Softball fields and horseshoe pits
A 10-acre pond with swimming, fishing, a beach area, and shaded picnic ramadas
For information about reserving facilities for special events , please contact Inyo County Parks & Recreation.
Millpond Campground is Concessionaire Operated
For more information please contact the Concessionaire 760.873.5342 or visit their web page : Brown's Campgrounds

A carousel is a rotating set of images, rotation stops on keyboard focus on carousel tab controls or hovering the mouse pointer over images. Use the tabs or the previous and next buttons to change the displayed slide.
Reservations, Fees & Rates
Camping Fees.
Camping fees are posted at each campground. All camping fees are per vehicle per night and are subject to change without notice. Camp Fees are $14.00 per night per vehicle. Camping fees at Glacier View, Brown's Town, Millpond and Tecopa Hot Springs campground are established by the concessionaire.
The following campgrounds have Automated Pay Stations that accept credit cards or cash:
Diaz Lake, Pleasant Valley, Baker Creek, Taboose Creek, Tinnemaha Creek and Portuguese Joe Campgrounds.
All County operated campgrounds will accommodate 45' RV's and most campsites will accommodate even the larger units. No showers or hook-ups are available at the County campgrounds. The elevation of each County operated campground is roughly 4,100 feet.
Fishing is allowed all year long in the Owen's River. Regular fishing season for creeks, streams and lakes is the last Saturday in April until November 15th.
Fishing licenses are required. Anyone 16 years and older must have a fishing license.
Services are available for black and gray removal. Contact Park Attendant. Available in spring and summer only.
Campgrounds are dog friendly.
Camping Reservations. You can now make reservations at . https://www.reserveamerica.com/ for all Inyo County campgrounds

How to Make Coffee While Camping
How to Make Coffee While Camping
Relaxing at your campsite and sipping your morning coffee as the day begins is a treasured moment on any camping trip. There are plenty of ways to learn how to make coffee while camping and we have highlighted five sure-fire favorites below.
Recommended: Camping Breakfast Ideas
1. Percolator Camping Coffee
If the question is how to make coffee while camping like grandma did? – then percolator coffee is surely the answer. This style of coffee requires a percolator coffee pot, which looks like a kettle and includes a press and filter inside. The result is a robust, if not sometimes bitter coffee, with the grinds completely separated from the water.
Fill the bottom chamber with cold water and the basket with coarse coffee grinds – about 1.5 tablespoons per cup of water
Secure the top of the percolator and put on a heat source set at about medium-high heat.
Bring to a boil and simmer for ten minutes.
Pour your cup of Joe.
Recommended: Great Summer RV Trips for Families
2. Pre-Packaged/Steeped Camping Coffee
When it is time to level up on the coffee flavor, while also minimizing the items you need to make coffee while camping, then steeped coffee is the way to go. You read that right. This coffee comes in a pouch and is brewed much like how you would steep an individual tea bag. Wildland Coffee is leading the way in the easy-to-make and tasty campsite coffee revolution, and Apex Club members get a discount. This method is great for any camping situation, and especially so for backpackers or those camping light on equipment.
To make steeped coffee simply:
Heat 8 ounces of water to almost a boil.
Add a bag of coffee and steep for eight minutes.
Remove the bag and sip away!
3. French Press Camping Coffee
French press coffee delivers fantastic flavor when done right. The trick is using medium ground grinds. Too fine a grind and you will end up with a muddy mess. Too coarse a grind and you will lose out on flavor. You can bring the tried-and-true glass french press but keep in mind that it is delicate and may not be durable enough for your camping trip. A plastic French press may be a better option for making coffee while camping, although in either case, a French press does take up some room and is not ideal for campers who need to go light with their equipment.
How to make coffee while camping with a French press coffee requires:
Heat water to a near boil.
Remove the plunger and add medium ground coffee to the chamber, about 1.5 tablespoons per cup of water.
Pour water into the chamber and stir grinds in water for about 10 seconds.
Insert the plunger and press down so it rests just above the water.
Let the coffee brew for about 4 minutes.
Slowly push down on the plunger until it reaches the bottom of the chamber.
Pour and enjoy
Recommended: Campgrounds with Boat Launches Across the US
4. AeroPress Camping Coffee
An AeroPress makes consistently outstanding coffee and is a favorite coffee-making contraption among coffee lovers. An AeroPress consists of a few relatively small plastic pieces, and a paper or mesh reusable filter. With its straightforward useability and packability, an AeroPress works well for many camping situations (although not backpacking). One drawback with an AeroPress is that you can only make one cup of Joe at a time.
How to make coffee while camping with an AeroPress, simply:
Heat water to a near boil.
Insert the filter in basket and twist basket onto the brew chamber.
Place the brew chamber with the basket over your mug.
Add finely-ground coffee into the chamber (about 1.5 tablespoons per cup).
Fill the chamber with hot water.
Stir the water and grounds for about 10 seconds.
Insert the plunger and leave at the top. Let coffee brew for about 1 minute.
Press plunger down so coffee comes directly into the mug.
5. Cowboy Coffee
This is the classic, traditional way to make backcountry coffee. While you’ll get points for the ruggedness factor of cowboy coffee, the acrid taste, and remnant grinds may not be preferred for some.
To make cowboy coffee:
Bring water to a boil in a kettle.
Add coarsely-ground coffee grinds, one tablespoon per 1.5 cups of water.
Stir the grinds and let the kettle boil for two minutes.
Remove the kettle from heat.
Remove the grinds by skimming the top of the water, or adding about 1oz of cold water and waiting a minute for the grinds to settle. (In the olden days, cowboys would also add eggshells to the kettle to keep the grounds down and enhance the flavor.)
Pour your cup and enjoy!
Are you ready for your adventure? Plan your camping trip!

Camping Trip Ideas for Couples
Camping Trip Ideas for Couples
Whether you and your partner are both avid campers or have never gone before, we are all for you taking a camping trip . Couples who share common interests or try new activities together deepen their bond. To get you inspired to head out into the wilderness for some couple fun, here are camping trip ideas for couples:
Stargaze and camp
Glamping
Cook a fancy meal outdoors
Take a tropical (camping) vacation
Soak in natural hot springs
Cuddle up to rugged mountain scenery
Recommended: Valentine’s Day Adventures
1. Sit Back and Stargaze
Where to Go: Cherry Springs State Park , Pennsylvania
Cherry Springs State Park is named after the cherry trees that bloom here in spring, but it is better known as a stargazers’ paradise. The park’s dark skies beckon novice and professional astronomers far and wide. With light pollution inhibiting our ability to see celestial splendor in many parts of the country, dark night skies are seen by many as a natural resource. In 2000, the Pennsylvania Department of Conservation and Natural Resources declared Cherry Springs State Park the first “Dark Sky Park,” ensuring its continued status as a dark sky refuge.
Come to Cherry Springs State Park with your loved one and kick back and take in the beauty of the cosmos. There are educational events and an “astronomer’s pass” if you want to learn more about the heavens.
Book a Campsite
2. Unwind at a Romantic Glamp Site
Where to Go: Dale Hollow Lake State Resort Park , Kentucky
For partners not into roughing it, our camping trip ideas for couples are glamping trips! Glamping allows you more amenities than traditional tent camping. Each of the six cabins at Dale Hollow Lake State Resort Park is fully furnished with a full bed and heating and air conditioning. There is running water available outside the cabin, and three bathhouses are located nearby.
Make your glamping trip extra romantic by bringing along your own lights (fairy lights are fun and romantic). Consider bringing along your own bedding to amp up the comfort factor and some games to play. There is plenty to do at this park too, including a marina with a boat ramp and an 18-hole championship golf course. Hit the trails on foot or horseback that take you through rolling forests.
Reserve a Cabin
Recommended: How to Go from Camping to Glamping
3. Cook a Fancy Meal
Where to Go: Don Carter State Park , Georgia
Just because you are camping doesn’t mean you can’t enjoy a nice romantic meal together. If you are up for it, make it a three-course meal with an appetizer, entree, and dessert. Choose whatever is in your comfort zone for cooking and of course foods that your partner loves.
Cooking while camping is all about meal prep, so cut, dice, and pre-cook what you can in advance. The very adventurous can do it over the campfire, but most of us will need a little more help with modern conveniences. The cottages at Don Carter State Park have a fully equipped kitchen with dishes, utensils, pots and pans, a coffee maker, and a microwave. The cottages have plenty of other nice amenities like wood-burning fireplaces and two queen-sized beds.
Reserve a Cottage
Recommended: Snowboard and Ski Cabin Trip Ideas
4. Take a Time Out in the Tropics
Where to Go: Sunshine Key RV Resort and Marina , Florida
What is more romantic than a beach getaway with your honey? Bare feet in the sand, the warm sun on your back, and the sweet tropical breeze sweeping off the sea – who doesn’t love that?
Among the all-star camping trip ideas for couples is a stay at Big Pine Key RV Park ,past the Seven Mile Bridge at mile marker 33 on the Overseas Hwy. This Florida Keys gem is famous for the National Key Deer Refuge and proximity to Everglades National Park. Enjoy your vacation fishing, boating, and exploring the local wildlife. Or simply stare at the stunningly clear, blue waters with your loved one by side – especially at sunset!
Reserve Your Campsite Now
Recommended: Some of the Best Natural Hot Springs in North America
5. Cuddle Up in Rugged, Romantic Scenery
Where to Go: Ridgway State Park , Colorado
If you are looking for an Alpine retreat without the flight to Europe, look no further than Ridgway State Park. Set in a soaring expanse of the Rocky Mountains nicknamed the “Switzerland of America,” Ridgway State Park has all of the rugged beauty you would expect of majestic high-mountain scenery: rocky peaks, wide meadows, meandering rivers, and deep forests. Among the classic camping trip ideas for couples, here you can go for a hike, spot the diverse species of wildlife, and breathe in the fresh mountain air. The park has 262 sites, including three yurts, and is open all year long.
Reserve Your Spot Today
Are you ready for your adventure? Plan your camping trip!

Incredible Island Camping Getaways
Incredible Island Camping Getaways
Did you know that there are plenty of island getaways off the coast of the U.S. to suit every kind of beachgoer? And the best news of all is that camping can make an island getaway both fun and affordable. We rounded up a few great island camping destinations so all you have to do is pack your swimsuit, sunglasses, and camping gear — and go.
Add these island camping getaways to your bucket list.
1. Hammocks Beach State Park , North Carolina
A 3-mile long undeveloped barrier island off the coast of North Carolina, Bear Island is accessible only by ferry or personal watercraft (canoe or kayak). If you’re looking for a place to get away from it all, you won’t find a more relaxing and undisturbed stretch of coastline anywhere. Camping on Bear Island is primitive, but it’s that kind of basics-only vibe that makes the island so special.
Stay the Night
2. Skidway Island State Park , Georgia
A small barrier island off the coast of Savannah, Georgia, Tybee Island is known for its wide, sandy beaches and still-functioning 18th-century lighthouse. Its close location to Savannah means that it’s an easy day trip into the city to check out all of Savannah’s historic sites. A camping trip to Tybee Island truly is a southern getaway that offers the best of the city and the sea.
Make a Reservation
Recommended: Great Places to Camp on the Beach
3. Fishermens Memorial State Park , Rhode Island
In the state of Rhode Island, Fishermen’s State Park has the feel of a seaside village atmosphere. Visitors will find neatly trimmed grass, tree-lined paths, and activities for the whole family. Whether you are looking for a place to pitch a tent and enjoy a campfire, or park your RV and play some basketball or tennis. Plus the campground has over 180 campsites to choose from.
Plan Your Adventure
Recommended: 15 Natural Attractions You Have to See to Believe
4. Mustang Island State Park , Texas
An 18-mile long barrier island off of the gulf coast of Texas, Mustang Island is well-known as a great place to sunbathe, search for seashells, surf in the warm ocean water or explore in a kayak. For a “traditional” sun and surf camping experience, it doesn’t get any better than Mustang Island.
Plan Your Visit
5. Glen Island Campground , New York
The Lake George Islands campsites are divided into three groups, Glen Island, Long Island, and Narrow Island offering several boat-in campsite options. Most sites are well-forested and private, offering a great getaway experience. All sites have a dock for at least one boat, a fireplace, a picnic table, and a toilet facility. All types of watercraft are welcome on the lake, and salmon and lake trout fishing is available. Back on land, make sure to explore over 50 miles of hiking trails leading to mountains overlooking the lake and to remote mountain ponds.

Welcome to Inyo County Parks & Recreation!
Reservations for all Inyo County campgrounds can be made at ReserveAmerica.com .
Inyo County Parks & Recreation is proud to offer and maintain fifteen beautiful parks and campgrounds for both residents and visitors. Each county-operated campground features a flowing creek in a rustic setting, creating a memorable outdoor experience.
Several of our lower-elevation campgrounds provide excellent fishing opportunities, with creeks regularly stocked with trout during the season—all conveniently located along U.S. Highway 395.
Independence Creek Campground sites 16–29 are closed until further notice due to a damaged bridge that provides access to this area. For the safety of all visitors, these sites will remain inaccessible while repairs are underway.
We appreciate your patience and understanding, and we will provide updates as soon as more information becomes available.
For questions or alternative site availability, please contact the campground office.
Pleasant Valley Campground offers year-round fishing in the Owens River.
Diaz Lake Campground features an 80-acre lake ideal for fishing, boating, and water sports. Shore fishing is open year-round, and a valid CA fishing license is required.
The Millpond Recreation Area spans over 120 acres and offers a wide variety of amenities, including:
A new disc golf course
Tennis courts
Play equipment
A gazebo for special events
Softball fields and horseshoe pits
A 10-acre pond with swimming, fishing, a beach area, and shaded picnic ramadas
For information about reserving facilities for special events , please contact Inyo County Parks & Recreation.
Millpond Campground is Concessionaire Operated
For more information please contact the Concessionaire 760.873.5342 or visit their web page : Brown's Campgrounds

Reservations, Fees & Rates
Camping Fees.
Camping fees are posted at each campground. All camping fees are per vehicle per night and are subject to change without notice. Camp Fees are $14.00 per night per vehicle. Camping fees at Glacier View, Brown's Town, Millpond and Tecopa Hot Springs campground are established by the concessionaire.
The following campgrounds have Automated Pay Stations that accept credit cards or cash:
Diaz Lake, Pleasant Valley, Baker Creek, Taboose Creek, Tinnemaha Creek and Portuguese Joe Campgrounds.
All County operated campgrounds will accommodate 45' RV's and most campsites will accommodate even the larger units. No showers or hook-ups are available at the County campgrounds. The elevation of each County operated campground is roughly 4,100 feet.
Fishing is allowed all year long in the Owen's River. Regular fishing season for creeks, streams and lakes is the last Saturday in April until November 15th.
Fishing licenses are required. Anyone 16 years and older must have a fishing license.
Services are available for black and gray removal. Contact Park Attendant. Available in spring and summer only.
Campgrounds are dog friendly.
Camping Reservations. You can now make reservations at . https://www.reserveamerica.com/ for all Inyo County campgrounds

How to Make Coffee While Camping
How to Make Coffee While Camping
Relaxing at your campsite and sipping your morning coffee as the day begins is a treasured moment on any camping trip. There are plenty of ways to learn how to make coffee while camping and we have highlighted five sure-fire favorites below.
Recommended: Camping Breakfast Ideas
1. Percolator Camping Coffee
If the question is how to make coffee while camping like grandma did? – then percolator coffee is surely the answer. This style of coffee requires a percolator coffee pot, which looks like a kettle and includes a press and filter inside. The result is a robust, if not sometimes bitter coffee, with the grinds completely separated from the water.
Fill the bottom chamber with cold water and the basket with coarse coffee grinds – about 1.5 tablespoons per cup of water
Secure the top of the percolator and put on a heat source set at about medium-high heat.
Bring to a boil and simmer for ten minutes.
Pour your cup of Joe.
Recommended: Great Summer RV Trips for Families
2. Pre-Packaged/Steeped Camping Coffee
When it is time to level up on the coffee flavor, while also minimizing the items you need to make coffee while camping, then steeped coffee is the way to go. You read that right. This coffee comes in a pouch and is brewed much like how you would steep an individual tea bag. Wildland Coffee is leading the way in the easy-to-make and tasty campsite coffee revolution, and Apex Club members get a discount. This method is great for any camping situation, and especially so for backpackers or those camping light on equipment.
To make steeped coffee simply:
Heat 8 ounces of water to almost a boil.
Add a bag of coffee and steep for eight minutes.
Remove the bag and sip away!
3. French Press Camping Coffee
French press coffee delivers fantastic flavor when done right. The trick is using medium ground grinds. Too fine a grind and you will end up with a muddy mess. Too coarse a grind and you will lose out on flavor. You can bring the tried-and-true glass french press but keep in mind that it is delicate and may not be durable enough for your camping trip. A plastic French press may be a better option for making coffee while camping, although in either case, a French press does take up some room and is not ideal for campers who need to go light with their equipment.
How to make coffee while camping with a French press coffee requires:
Heat water to a near boil.
Remove the plunger and add medium ground coffee to the chamber, about 1.5 tablespoons per cup of water.
Pour water into the chamber and stir grinds in water for about 10 seconds.
Insert the plunger and press down so it rests just above the water.
Let the coffee brew for about 4 minutes.
Slowly push down on the plunger until it reaches the bottom of the chamber.
Pour and enjoy
Recommended: Campgrounds with Boat Launches Across the US
4. AeroPress Camping Coffee
An AeroPress makes consistently outstanding coffee and is a favorite coffee-making contraption among coffee lovers. An AeroPress consists of a few relatively small plastic pieces, and a paper or mesh reusable filter. With its straightforward useability and packability, an AeroPress works well for many camping situations (although not backpacking). One drawback with an AeroPress is that you can only make one cup of Joe at a time.
How to make coffee while camping with an AeroPress, simply:
Heat water to a near boil.
Insert the filter in basket and twist basket onto the brew chamber.
Place the brew chamber with the basket over your mug.
Add finely-ground coffee into the chamber (about 1.5 tablespoons per cup).
Fill the chamber with hot water.
Stir the water and grounds for about 10 seconds.
Insert the plunger and leave at the top. Let coffee brew for about 1 minute.
Press plunger down so coffee comes directly into the mug.
5. Cowboy Coffee
This is the classic, traditional way to make backcountry coffee. While you’ll get points for the ruggedness factor of cowboy coffee, the acrid taste, and remnant grinds may not be preferred for some.
To make cowboy coffee:
Bring water to a boil in a kettle.
Add coarsely-ground coffee grinds, one tablespoon per 1.5 cups of water.
Stir the grinds and let the kettle boil for two minutes.
Remove the kettle from heat.
Remove the grinds by skimming the top of the water, or adding about 1oz of cold water and waiting a minute for the grinds to settle. (In the olden days, cowboys would also add eggshells to the kettle to keep the grounds down and enhance the flavor.)
Pour your cup and enjoy!

Welcome to Inyo County Parks & Recreation!
Reservations for all Inyo County campgrounds can be made at ReserveAmerica.com .
Inyo County Parks & Recreation is proud to offer and maintain fifteen beautiful parks and campgrounds for both residents and visitors. Each county-operated campground features a flowing creek in a rustic setting, creating a memorable outdoor experience.
Several of our lower-elevation campgrounds provide excellent fishing opportunities, with creeks regularly stocked with trout during the season—all conveniently located along U.S. Highway 395.
Independence Creek Campground sites 16–29 are closed until further notice due to a damaged bridge that provides access to this area. For the safety of all visitors, these sites will remain inaccessible while repairs are underway.
We appreciate your patience and understanding, and we will provide updates as soon as more information becomes available.
For questions or alternative site availability, please contact the campground office.
Pleasant Valley Campground offers year-round fishing in the Owens River.
Diaz Lake Campground features an 80-acre lake ideal for fishing, boating, and water sports. Shore fishing is open year-round, and a valid CA fishing license is required.
The Millpond Recreation Area spans over 120 acres and offers a wide variety of amenities, including:
A new disc golf course
Tennis courts
Play equipment
A gazebo for special events
Softball fields and horseshoe pits
A 10-acre pond with swimming, fishing, a beach area, and shaded picnic ramadas
For information about reserving facilities for special events , please contact Inyo County Parks & Recreation.
Millpond Campground is Concessionaire Operated
For more information please contact the Concessionaire 760.873.5342 or visit their web page : Brown's Campgrounds

Reservations, Fees & Rates
Camping Fees.
Camping fees are posted at each campground. All camping fees are per vehicle per night and are subject to change without notice. Camp Fees are $14.00 per night per vehicle. Camping fees at Glacier View, Brown's Town, Millpond and Tecopa Hot Springs campground are established by the concessionaire.
The following campgrounds have Automated Pay Stations that accept credit cards or cash:
Diaz Lake, Pleasant Valley, Baker Creek, Taboose Creek, Tinnemaha Creek and Portuguese Joe Campgrounds.
All County operated campgrounds will accommodate 45' RV's and most campsites will accommodate even the larger units. No showers or hook-ups are available at the County campgrounds. The elevation of each County operated campground is roughly 4,100 feet.
Fishing is allowed all year long in the Owen's River. Regular fishing season for creeks, streams and lakes is the last Saturday in April until November 15th.
Fishing licenses are required. Anyone 16 years and older must have a fishing license.
Services are available for black and gray removal. Contact Park Attendant. Available in spring and summer only.
Campgrounds are dog friendly.
Camping Reservations. You can now make reservations at . https://www.reserveamerica.com/ for all Inyo County campgrounds

How to Make Coffee While Camping
How to Make Coffee While Camping
Relaxing at your campsite and sipping your morning coffee as the day begins is a treasured moment on any camping trip. There are plenty of ways to learn how to make coffee while camping and we have highlighted five sure-fire favorites below.
Recommended: Camping Breakfast Ideas
1. Percolator Camping Coffee
If the question is how to make coffee while camping like grandma did? – then percolator coffee is surely the answer. This style of coffee requires a percolator coffee pot, which looks like a kettle and includes a press and filter inside. The result is a robust, if not sometimes bitter coffee, with the grinds completely separated from the water.
Fill the bottom chamber with cold water and the basket with coarse coffee grinds – about 1.5 tablespoons per cup of water
Secure the top of the percolator and put on a heat source set at about medium-high heat.
Bring to a boil and simmer for ten minutes.
Pour your cup of Joe.
Recommended: Great Summer RV Trips for Families
2. Pre-Packaged/Steeped Camping Coffee
When it is time to level up on the coffee flavor, while also minimizing the items you need to make coffee while camping, then steeped coffee is the way to go. You read that right. This coffee comes in a pouch and is brewed much like how you would steep an individual tea bag. Wildland Coffee is leading the way in the easy-to-make and tasty campsite coffee revolution, and Apex Club members get a discount. This method is great for any camping situation, and especially so for backpackers or those camping light on equipment.
To make steeped coffee simply:
Heat 8 ounces of water to almost a boil.
Add a bag of coffee and steep for eight minutes.
Remove the bag and sip away!
3. French Press Camping Coffee
French press coffee delivers fantastic flavor when done right. The trick is using medium ground grinds. Too fine a grind and you will end up with a muddy mess. Too coarse a grind and you will lose out on flavor. You can bring the tried-and-true glass french press but keep in mind that it is delicate and may not be durable enough for your camping trip. A plastic French press may be a better option for making coffee while camping, although in either case, a French press does take up some room and is not ideal for campers who need to go light with their equipment.
How to make coffee while camping with a French press coffee requires:
Heat water to a near boil.
Remove the plunger and add medium ground coffee to the chamber, about 1.5 tablespoons per cup of water.
Pour water into the chamber and stir grinds in water for about 10 seconds.
Insert the plunger and press down so it rests just above the water.
Let the coffee brew for about 4 minutes.
Slowly push down on the plunger until it reaches the bottom of the chamber.
Pour and enjoy
Recommended: Campgrounds with Boat Launches Across the US
4. AeroPress Camping Coffee
An AeroPress makes consistently outstanding coffee and is a favorite coffee-making contraption among coffee lovers. An AeroPress consists of a few relatively small plastic pieces, and a paper or mesh reusable filter. With its straightforward useability and packability, an AeroPress works well for many camping situations (although not backpacking). One drawback with an AeroPress is that you can only make one cup of Joe at a time.
How to make coffee while camping with an AeroPress, simply:
Heat water to a near boil.
Insert the filter in basket and twist basket onto the brew chamber.
Place the brew chamber with the basket over your mug.
Add finely-ground coffee into the chamber (about 1.5 tablespoons per cup).
Fill the chamber with hot water.
Stir the water and grounds for about 10 seconds.
Insert the plunger and leave at the top. Let coffee brew for about 1 minute.
Press plunger down so coffee comes directly into the mug.
5. Cowboy Coffee
This is the classic, traditional way to make backcountry coffee. While you’ll get points for the ruggedness factor of cowboy coffee, the acrid taste, and remnant grinds may not be preferred for some.
To make cowboy coffee:
Bring water to a boil in a kettle.
Add coarsely-ground coffee grinds, one tablespoon per 1.5 cups of water.
Stir the grinds and let the kettle boil for two minutes.
Remove the kettle from heat.
Remove the grinds by skimming the top of the water, or adding about 1oz of cold water and waiting a minute for the grinds to settle. (In the olden days, cowboys would also add eggshells to the kettle to keep the grounds down and enhance the flavor.)
Pour your cup and enjoy!
Are you ready for your adventure? Plan your camping trip!

DIAZ LAKE CAMPGROUND
PLEASE CLICK FOR IMPORTANT INFORMATION ABOUT THE GOLDEN MUSSELL: https://easternsierrawid.com/
CAMPFIRES ARE CURRENTLY ALLOWED ONLY IN THE PROVIDED METAL FIRE RINGS
You can make a reservation for this campground at www.reserveamerica.com
First come, first serve sites are also available.
Location
Three miles south of Lone Pine, CA on U.S. 395.
Amenities
Swimming, fishing, water skiing, picnicking, boating, grills, fire rings, tables, vault toilets, play equipment. 100 spaces, 80-acre lake. Camping spaces are available for large RV's. No shower facilities within the campground. No hook-ups. Limited water spigots are available throughout the campground.
ATV riding is NOT allowed inside the campground. ATV trails are located out the back gate of the campground.
Six people allowed per site.
Sites 44, 45 and 46 are group sites that accommodate 15 people. $35 per night.
Fee Information
Automated Pay Stations accept credit cards and cash
$14 per site/vehicle per night
Additional vehicle: $5.00 per night
$10 Daily Rate for Motorized Watercraft
NOTICE:
WATERCRAFT IN INYO COUNTY ARE REQUIRED TO UNDERGO INSPECTION AND DECONTAMINATION FOR THE INVASIVE MUSSEL SPECIES.
For more information regarding boat inspection requirements, please visit Inyo County Code Chapter 10.70.
Diaz Lake Boating Schedule
🚤 Diaz Lake Motorized Watercraft Opening – May 15, 2026
Get ready for a great season on the water! Motorized watercraft use at Diaz Lake officially opens on May 15, 2026 . Visitors can enjoy boating, fishing, and stunning Sierra views as the summer kicks off. Motorized watercraft use will be closing for the season starting November 1st, 2026.
Please remember to follow all posted lake regulations and safety guidelines. We look forward to welcoming you back for another year of outdoor fun at Diaz Lake!
For questions and concerns, please contact the Parks and Recreation Manager:
Phone: (760) 614-1326
Email: Jbriceno@inyocounty.us
Boating Hours
Monday thru Sunday – 8am to 2:30pm
Open year round for kayaks, canoes and non-motorized watercraft.
Shore fishing is allowed at Diaz Lake all year. California Fishing license is required for 16 years old and older.
ADA fishing deck located near the boat launch ramp.
If you require further information, please call 760-873-5577 or email Inyo Parks & Recreation

Reservations, Fees & Rates
Camping Fees.
Camping fees are posted at each campground. All camping fees are per vehicle per night and are subject to change without notice. Camp Fees are $14.00 per night per vehicle. Camping fees at Glacier View, Brown's Town, Millpond and Tecopa Hot Springs campground are established by the concessionaire.
The following campgrounds have Automated Pay Stations that accept credit cards or cash:
Diaz Lake, Pleasant Valley, Baker Creek, Taboose Creek, Tinnemaha Creek and Portuguese Joe Campgrounds.
All County operated campgrounds will accommodate 45' RV's and most campsites will accommodate even the larger units. No showers or hook-ups are available at the County campgrounds. The elevation of each County operated campground is roughly 4,100 feet.
Fishing is allowed all year long in the Owen's River. Regular fishing season for creeks, streams and lakes is the last Saturday in April until November 15th.
Fishing licenses are required. Anyone 16 years and older must have a fishing license.
Services are available for black and gray removal. Contact Park Attendant. Available in spring and summer only.
Campgrounds are dog friendly.
Camping Reservations. You can now make reservations at . https://www.reserveamerica.com/ for all Inyo County campgrounds

Campground Directory - ReserveAmerica
Skip to main content
Campground Directory
There are thousands of public and privately-owned campgrounds catering to the needs of millions of campers using tents, travel trailers, motor homes or other types of RVs. Our campground directory will describe each, as to location, season, rates and amenities.
The Followings are the major types of campgrounds:
State Agencies
Colorado Parks and Wildlife
Colorado Parks & Wildlife (CPW) has partnered with Aspira since 1993. In 2018, CPW implemented IPAWS (Integrated Parks and Wildlife System), marking the industry's first fully integrated parks and licensing system. Aspira manages this comprehensive platform that allows users to purchase fishing and hunting licenses, campground reservations, vehicle registrations, hunting reservations, and license draws through a single cart system, serving customers both online and through 400+ license agent locations. A significant enhancement to IPAWS was the 2023 introduction of the Keep Colorado Wild Pass, which integrates with the state's DMV system and has attracted over 2 million participants by offering discounted state park access during vehicle registration renewal.
Connecticut Department of Energy and Environmental Protection
A partner for over 25 years, Connecticut offers campgrounds in thirteen state parks or forests with over 1,400 campsites. Camping areas can be found in a variety settings including shadowy woodlands, sandy shoreline beaches, and secluded islands. A unique opportunity for visitors includes tours through the historic Gillette Castle. This medieval castle is the former home of William Gillette, most famous for his acting role portraying Sherlock Holmes. Aspira has implemented a QR code at the entrance allowing for payment electronically at Gillette Castle and all day-use areas across the state.
Delaware State Parks
Delaware State Parks has progressively expanded their utilization of Aspira's services to include camping reservations, point of sale, ticketing for both tours and waterpark access, passes and permits, and advanced beach access reservations. The partnership notably features an innovative surf fishing permit program implemented in 2023, which uses daily entrance functionality to balance conservation needs with public access through an advanced reservation system. As a 2021 National Gold Medal Award recipient for Excellence in Parks and Recreation Management, Delaware State Parks has achieved significant growth in camping, cabin stays, and overall park attendance throughout their time with Aspira.
Georgia State Parks & Historic Sites
Georgia offers over 2,400 campsites including tent-only areas, RV pull-thru sites, primitive camping, and group camping. Tent/Trailer/RV sites offer electrical and water hook-ups, grills or fire rings, and picnic tables. Aspira partners with Georgia State Parks and Historic Sites to offer a private white label website, reservation systems, and hardware such as desktops, monitors, and receipt printers. Georgia is one of the first states to test out tablets provided by Aspira to sell point of sale items and check-in visitors outside of their visitor centers.
Indiana Department of Natural Resources
Aspira's partnership with Indiana State Parks spans over two decades. With more than 7,000 campsites, 200+ cabins, multiple cottages, group camps, and shelters, Indiana State Parks is one of Aspira's largest camping providers. Aspira helped launch point of sale across the state, totaling more than 140 stations. Indiana Dunes State Parks features three miles of dune lined shores on Lake Michigan and was featured as one of the best places to hike in Indiana by USA Today.
Iowa State Parks
Entering the 15th year of partnership with Aspira, Iowa State Parks offers camping enthusiasts a wide variety of camping opportunities in 55 parks, recreation areas, and state forests. If camping isn't your style, try out a camping cabin, yurt, or family cabin. Aspria provides accommodation and permit solutions, along with credit card terminals for their hardware needs.
Kansas Department of Wildlife and Parks
Kansas has 28 state parks that offer a variety of hiking, camping, wildlife watching, fishing, bike riding, horseback riding, and other activities for visitors. Most offer utility and primitive camping and access to lakes, trails, wildlife areas, and preserved natural areas. Kansas utilizes many of Aspira's flagship features, from gift cards to point of sale. They were the driver behind Aspira's first branded camping app, Campit KS, which allows campers to search for campsites and book directly. Aspira also helps release all of Kansas's inventory through two rush events in mid-December each year.
Kentucky Department of Parks
The Kentucky state park system includes 52 parks and one interstate park with facilities for meetings and conferences, luxury accommodations, camping, golf, education, and more. Kentucky utilizes many of Aspira's offerings, including centralized camping reservations and registrations, point of sale, financial management, marketing services, and support services.
Massachusetts Department of Conservation and Recreation
For over 25 years, Aspira has partnered with Massachusetts to oversee 450,000 acres of the state's parks and forests, beaches, bike trails, watersheds, dams, and parkways. The department also protects land and resources on privately and municipally held land. Aspira provides a commercial, off-the-shelf system for Massachusetts, while ensuring the park system's custom business rules such as minimum stay lengths and resident vs. non-resident fees are automatically calculated and implemented during the booking process.
Montana State Parks
Since 2011, Montana State Parks has worked with Aspira to provide consumer access to their state parks. Over time, Montana has engaged Aspira to support management of camping and day-use reservations for families and groups, marina slip reservations for boaters and anglers, and tour and ticket purchase for Montana State Park attractions.
Nebraska Game and Parks Commission
Nebraska has been one of Aspira's partners since 2007. Nebraska's park system encompasses 86 areas across the state, with popular activities such as boating, hiking, and RV and tent camping. Aspira provides Nebraska’s reservation and point of sale solutions. In 2017, Aspira integrated Nebraska’s Poynt payment processing system with the Aspira One software program.
New Hampshire Division of Parks and Recreation
Collaborating since 2007, Aspira assists New Hampshire State Parks with managing over 73 state parks, campgrounds, historic sites, natural areas, and thousands of miles of trails. New Hampshire takes advantage of a variety of Aspira's features, including check-in software, venue management, ticketing, point of sale, and enhanced insights into occupancy, revenue, and attendance.
New Mexico State Parks
Since 2007, Aspira has helped New Mexico State Parks manage 35 diverse state parks (28 of which have camping facilities) for campers to explore, including cool lakes, mountain forests, canyons, desert beauty, and fascinating historical sites. In 2024, Aspira implemented rental functionality for ADA Trackchair rentals at Manzano Mountains State Park. Since going live with this feature, New Mexico parks leadership have received excellent feedback from visitors for this initiative.
New York State Department of Environmental Conservation & Office of Parks Recreation and Historic Preservation
New York State Parks welcomes millions of visitors each year to enjoy the natural, environmental, historic, and cultural resources of the State. Accommodations offered include campsites, cabins, cottages, yurts, and backcountry camping areas for overnight stays. Aspira provides the solutions to reserve these overnight accommodations, along with day-use reservations such as picnic areas, pavilions, and marinas. Aspira provides the solutions for New York State Parks to operate a customer loyalty program which awards points that can be used toward overnight reservations.
North Carolina State Parks
North Carolina State Parks provides recreational activities to more than 500,000 customers each year and provides access to 36 parks across the state. North Carolina provides lodging, camping, and events to their customers, the latter using a customized version of the system. Aspira partners with North Carolina State Parks to provide connectivity and point of sale access to all their parks and customers.
Oregon Parks and Recreation Department
A partnership that is nearly three decades in the making, Oregon’s state parks are among the most popular in the United States and consistently ranks among the 10 most visited in the nation. Aspira worked with Oregon to move their system away from a mail-in reservation system to a centralized system in the mid-90’s. Today, Oregon serves as one of the leaders in park-technology advancement and adoption.
Pennsylvania State Parks
Aspira partners with Pennsylvania State Parks to provide technology solutions for a wide range of facilities including cabins, yurts, deluxe cottages, and various campsite types, as well as 42 marinas with both transient (float-in) and seasonal slips. Pennsylvania utilizes Aspira's camping, marina, backpacking, and point of sale modules to facilitate unique offerings like river camping with itinerary planning for canoe and kayak enthusiasts.
Rhode Island Department of Environmental Management
Rhode Island offers 9 state park and forestry campgrounds with over 1,000 campsites located within in woodlands, freshwater lakes, and have some located minutes from Rhode Island's beautiful saltwater beaches. The sites range from primitive to developed sites with electric, water, and sewer hookups. In 2023, the state incorporated the Forestry division into Aspira's contract to provide opportunities for visitors to reserve equestrian and backcountry sites.
Texas Parks & Wildlife
Texas Parks & Wildlife Department (TPWD) has partnered with Aspira to enhance their operational capabilities across more than 80 state parks, historic sites, and natural areas. The system enables comprehensive visitor services including campground reservations, day-use bookings, activity reservations, and equipment rentals across Texas's diverse landscapes from desert terrain to pine forests. TPWD pioneered Aspira's innovative kiosk solution, which has served over 50,000 visitors through self-service check-ins and day-use pass purchases. The partnership leverages multiple of Aspira's products including private label website management, point of sale, and marketing to provide a complete park management solution.
Utah State Parks and Recreation
Aspira assists Utah State Parks with managing cabins, cottages, yurts, tiny homes, and more than 2,000 campsites. In 2024, Aspira integrated credit card on file functionality for many site types to help Utah Parks recoup money for any damages caused at their parks.
Private Campgrounds
Firefly Reservations
Firefly Reservations is a cloud-based reservation management solution designed for RV parks and campgrounds. The software lets customers make and pay for reservations online, and allows users to automate a variety of tasks such as sending emails and collecting payments for reservations & utilities.
Firefly Reservations enables the management of short term and long term reservations. Users can create interactive maps of their campground or RV park to display unit availability. Customers can select units and make reservations online through the custom-branded reservation portal, which can be linked to through a button embedded in existing websites. Automated emails allows users to communicate confirmations, reservation information, payment reminders, and other important notices with customers through customizable templates.
Firefly Reservations supports recurring and scheduled payments for monthly guests, storage unit fees, and other regular charges. Utilities can also be recorded and billed through the system, and one-off transactions can be processed through the built-in point of sale (POS). A self-serve kiosk lets customers check themselves in and make payments outside of office hours, and a guest portal for guests to mange their reservation, update payment methods, make payments, and view payment history at any time.
Private Campgrounds and Local Governments
Private Campgrounds and Local Governments provide the customers a number of different camping choices from private agencies across the country.
Other Agencies
Charleston County Park and Recreation Commission
As our campground guest, we invite you to enjoy the natural beauty of James Island County Park, with year-round enjoyment for the entire family. Our 643-acre park offers an abundance of exceptional recreation offerings and natural beauty and is just a short drive from historic downtown Charleston and area beaches.
East Bay Regional Park District, California
Manages 65 parks and 29 regional interpark trails in Alameda and Contra Costa counties.
Estes Valley Recreation and Park District
The Estes Valley Recreation and Park District is a public agency providing park management and recreation programs for members of the community and visitors to Estes Park, Colorado. The District manages 2 campgrounds, 2 golf courses, the marina on Lake Estes, the aquatic center, miles of recreational trails, an indoor and outdoor shooting range, multi-use park facilities that include ball fields, playgrounds, picnic areas, tennis courts, a youth center and a wide variety of recreational programs for all ages. Estes Park has been voted by the Weather Channel as being one of the best Family-Friendly Destinations in the nation and has also been recognized by Trip Advisor with a Traveller's Choice Award as being one of the top 25 destinations in the United States. For more information, please visit www.evrpd.com .
Florida Forest Service
Florida has one of the most extensive and well-managed state forest systems in the nation, with 37 state forests covering 1.1 million acres. Since 2017, Florida Forest Service and Aspira have partnered together to manage more than 80 campgrounds offering primitive to improved campsite experiences. From camping along waterways to hiking meandering trails through the forest, there is something for everyone at Florida’s state forests.
Inyo County Parks and Recreation
Inyo County is a land of fascinating extremes. Here you will find Mt. Whitney, the highest point in the lower 48 states, as well as, Death Valley, the lowest point in North America. Inyo’s seven campgrounds offer dramatic mountain and desert scenery with nearly 400 campsites in close proximity to six million acres of public lands for you to explore. Other natural wonders include the Alabama Hills and the Ancient Bristlecone Pine Forest where you will find the oldest living things on the planet. Activities include; historical sites, hiking, climbing, fishing, off-roading and skiing. Come visit Inyo County on the other side of California.
Kettle Creek Conservation Authority
Thank you for choosing to spend part of your summer with us! A haven for wildlife, and campers alike, the family-friendly conservation areas offer the best of the outdoors in a clean, well-maintained environment. No wonder the majority of our guests are repeat visitors.
Larimer County Department of Natural Resources, Colorado
Campsites, camper cabins, trails, reservoirs (Carter, Flatiron, Horsetooth, Pinewood) from the northern Front Range of the Rockies to Estes Park, Colorado.
NOVA Parks
NOVA Parks campgrounds are situated in two of its largest parks, Bull Run Regional Park in Centreville, VA and Pohick Bay Regional Park in Lorton VA. Each offers space for RV's, campsites with electrical and water hookups, tent sites and cabins. Enjoy all the great park amenities like water access, hiking, swimming and more. All of this while being close to Washington D.C. www.novaparks.com
Oconee County Parks (South Carolina)
Get Outside! Feel Alive! With over 200 campsites and the Mountain Lakes region of South Carolina as your playground, the Outdoors is Yours. South Cove and High Falls park are located along the shores of beautiful Lake Keowee and Chau-Ram park located sits along the Chauga River.
Ohio State Fair
The Ohio State Fair has been a favorite family tradition since 1850! Enjoy a variety of activities and exhibits including interactive educational activities, sporting competitions, a fine arts show, free entertainment stages, a free petting zoo, helicopter rides, a farm animal delivery room, roving performers, agricultural competitions, more than 60 fun rides, horse shows, an 8-acre natural resources park with free kiddie fishing and much more! You won't be able to resist all your favorite Fair goodies from any of the nearly 200 food vendors.
Josephine County Parks, Oregon
Has some of the most beautiful parks in the Pacific Northwest.
All but two camping parks are located on the world famous Rogue
River.
State Camping Highlights
Colorado Camping
Find breathtaking camping in Colorado. Hike, fish, bike, canoe and more at Colorado state parks, forests, and recreation areas. Start you adventure with the perfect campground, cabin, RV park or day use facility.
Georgia Camping
Visit the best Georgia campgrounds. Georgia state parks, forests, beaches and more offer a wide range of activities to help you create the perfect vacation. Check out the best Georgia camping options here.
Indiana Camping
Check out the best of Indiana camping. Located in the heart of the Midwest,
Indiana campgrounds and other facilities within the Indiana DNR offer a get-a-way
destination for Hoosiers and out-of-state visitors alike. Find tent camping and
RV park campgrounds, as well as hidden gems and cabin rentals.
New Hampshire Camping
Check out the best of New Hampshire camping. Find tent camping and RV park
campgrounds, as well as hidden gems and cabin rentals. Here you'll find some of
the best campgrounds and places to camp in New Hampshire.
New Mexico Camping
New Mexico has many diverse State Parks and camping areas to
explore, including cool lakes, mountain forests, canyons, desert
beauty and fascinating historical sites - even dinosaur tracks! Here
you'll find the best campgrounds and places to camp in New Mexico.
North Carolina Camping
North Carolina is blessed with beautiful beaches, majestic
mountains and countless rivers and streams in between. Here you'll
find the best campgrounds and places to camp in North Carolina.
New York Camping
Check out the best of New York camping. From the shores of Long Island to
the mighty Niagara Falls, New York's 179 state parks offer innumerous opportunities
to explore your natural surroundings, escape from the daily grind and discover
exciting new adventures.
Oregon Camping
Enjoy Oregon's 170 state parks and 362 miles of ocean shoreline with amazing cabin and yurt rentals and coastline camping locations.
Pennsylvania Camping
Experience some of the best camping and cabin rentals Pennsylvania has to offer with some top picks for parks to visit on your next Pennsylvania vacation.
Texas Camping
As the largest state in the continental US, Texas offers a broad and diverse expanse of camping opportunities and outdoor activities. Camping in Texas is available year-round in most areas, although we generally recommend your Texas camping trip take place in early Spring or late Fall to avoid hot summer temperatures.
